sentences.zh: 梅之煥，字彬父，麻城人，侍郎國楨從子也。

translations.literal: Mei Zhihuan, style Binfu, was a native of Macheng and a nephew of the Vice Minister Mei Guozhen.
translations.idiomatic: Mei Zhihuan, whose style name was Binfu, came from Macheng and was a nephew of Vice Minister Mei Guozhen.

sentences.zh: 年十四為諸生。

translations.literal: At fourteen he became a licentiate.
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen he became a licentiate.

sentences.zh: 御史行部閱武，之煥騎馬突教場。

translations.literal: When a censor toured the department to review military drill, Zhihuan rode his horse straight into the training ground.
translations.idiomatic: When a touring censor came to inspect military drill, Zhihuan galloped straight onto the parade ground.

sentences.zh: 御史怒，命與材官角射，九發九中，長揖上馬而去。

translations.literal: The censor was angry and ordered him to compete in archery with a military officer; nine shots, nine hits; he bowed with a long salute, mounted, and left.
translations.idiomatic: The censor was furious and ordered him to shoot against a military officer; he loosed nine arrows and hit nine times, then made a deep bow, mounted, and rode away.

sentences.zh: 萬歷三十二年舉進士，改庶吉士。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year of Wanli he passed the jinshi examination and was made a Hanlin bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-second year of the Wanli reign he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed a Hanlin bachelor.

sentences.zh: 居七年，授吏科給事中。

translations.literal: After seven years he was appointed supervising secretary in the Office of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: After seven years he was appointed supervising secretary in the Office of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 東廠太監李浚誣拷商人，之煥劾其罪。

translations.literal: The Eastern Depot eunuch Li Jun falsely tortured merchants; Zhihuan impeached him for the crime.
translations.idiomatic: When the Eastern Depot eunuch Li Jun falsely tortured merchants, Zhihuan impeached him for the crime.

sentences.zh: 尋上言：「今天下民窮餉匱，寇橫兵疲。

translations.literal: Soon after he memorialized: "Today the people are impoverished and supplies exhausted, bandits run rampant and the army is weary.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he memorialized the throne: "The empire today is exhausted—its people impoverished, its supplies spent, bandits rampant, and its armies weary.

sentences.zh: 言官舍國事爭時局，部曹舍職掌建空言，天下盡為虛文所束縛。

translations.literal: Censors abandon state affairs to wrangle over factional alignments; department officials abandon their duties to pile up empty words; the whole realm is bound by hollow formalities.
translations.idiomatic: Censors abandon state business to quarrel over factional alignments; department officials abandon their proper duties to heap up empty talk; the whole realm is strangled by hollow formalities.

sentences.zh: 有意振刷者，不曰生事，則曰苛求。

translations.literal: Those who wish to revive affairs are called either troublemakers or exacting.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who tries to set things right is called either a troublemaker or a nitpicker.

sentences.zh: 事未就而謗興，法未伸而怨集，豪傑灰心，庸人養拙，國事將不可為矣。

translations.literal: Before affairs are accomplished slander rises; before law is enforced resentment gathers; heroes lose heart, mediocrities cultivate incompetence—state affairs will soon be beyond remedy.
translations.idiomatic: Before a task is finished, slander begins; before justice is done, resentment piles up; men of talent lose heart, mediocrities cling to their dullness—and state affairs will soon be beyond saving.

sentences.zh: 請陛下嚴綜核以責實事，通言路以重紀綱，別臧否以惜人才，庶於國事有濟。」

translations.literal: I beg Your Majesty to enforce strict verification to demand real results, open the channels of speech to strengthen discipline, distinguish good and ill to cherish talent—then state affairs may be helped."
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to enforce strict verification so that real work is demanded, open the channels of memorializing so that discipline is strengthened, and distinguish merit from fault so that talent is cherished—only then may state affairs be helped."

sentences.zh: 時朝臣部黨角立，之煥廉觚自勝，嘗言：「附小人者必小人，附君子者未必君子。

translations.literal: At the time court ministers stood in rival factions; Zhihuan held himself aloof with integrity and once said: "Those who attach themselves to petty men are surely petty men; those who attach themselves to gentlemen are not necessarily gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: At that time court ministers stood in rival factions. Zhihuan held himself aloof with integrity and once said: "Those who attach themselves to petty men are surely petty men themselves; those who attach themselves to gentlemen are not necessarily gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 蠅之附驥，即千里猶蠅耳。」

translations.literal: A fly that clings to a thoroughbred, though it runs a thousand li, is still a fly."
translations.idiomatic: A fly that clings to a thousand-li steed is still a fly, even if it runs a thousand li with the horse."

sentences.zh: 時有追論故相張居正者，之煥曰：「使今日有綜名實、振紀綱如江陵者，訁翕訿之徒敢若此耶？」

translations.literal: When some pursued a posthumous reckoning with the former chief minister Zhang Juzheng, Zhihuan said: "If today there were one who, like Jiangling, coordinated names with realities and revived discipline, would the slanderers dare act like this?"
translations.idiomatic: When some pursued a posthumous reckoning with the former chief minister Zhang Juzheng, Zhihuan said: "If today there were someone who, like Jiangling, matched names to realities and revived discipline, would the carping slanderers dare behave like this?"

sentences.zh: 其持平不欲傅會人如此。

translations.literal: In this way he was even-handed and unwilling to curry favor with others.
translations.idiomatic: In this way he was even-handed and unwilling to curry favor with others.

sentences.zh: 出為廣東副使，擒誅豪民沈殺烈女者，民服其神。

translations.literal: He went out as vice commissioner of Guangdong, captured and executed a powerful local who had drowned a chaste woman, and the people revered his divine power.
translations.idiomatic: Sent out as vice commissioner of Guangdong, he captured and executed a powerful local who had drowned a chaste woman, and the people revered him as almost supernatural in his justice.

sentences.zh: 海寇袁進掠潮州，之煥扼海道，招散其黨，卒降進。

translations.literal: The sea bandit Yuan Jin raided Chaozhou; Zhihuan blocked the sea routes, recruited and dispersed his followers, and in the end Yuan Jin surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: When the sea bandit Yuan Jin raided Chaozhou, Zhihuan blocked the sea routes, recruited and dispersed his followers, and in the end Yuan Jin surrendered.

sentences.zh: 改視山東學政。

translations.literal: He was transferred to oversee educational administration in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to oversee educational administration in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 天啟元年以通政參議召遷太常少卿，擢右僉都御史，巡撫南、贛。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianqi he was summoned from his post as vice commissioner of communications, promoted to vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and then raised to right vice censor-in-chief to serve as grand coordinator of Nan and Gan.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianqi he was summoned from his post as vice commissioner of communications, promoted to vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and then raised to right vice censor-in-chief as grand coordinator of Nan and Gan.

sentences.zh: 丁內外艱，家居。

translations.literal: He observed mourning for both parents and lived at home.
translations.idiomatic: He observed mourning for both parents and retired to his home.

sentences.zh: 當此之時，魏、客亂政，應山楊漣首發忠賢之奸。

translations.literal: At this time Wei and Ke threw the government into disorder; Yingshan Yang Lian was the first to expose Zhongxian's villainy.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Wei Zhongxian and Lady Ke threw the government into disorder; Yang Lian of Yingshan was the first to expose Zhongxian's villainy.

sentences.zh: 忠賢恚甚，拷殺漣。

translations.literal: Zhongxian was furious beyond measure and tortured Lian to death.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxian was consumed with rage and tortured Lian to death.

sentences.zh: 由此悍然益誅鋤善類，忄買慀楚人矣。

translations.literal: From this he became ever bolder in hunting down and rooting out the good, and bore still greater enmity toward men of Chu.
translations.idiomatic: From this he became ever bolder in hunting down and rooting out the good, and bore still greater enmity toward men of Chu.

sentences.zh: 謂漣被逮時，過麻城，漣罪人也，之煥與盤桓流涕，當削籍，其實漣未嘗過麻城也。

translations.literal: It was said that when Lian was arrested he passed through Macheng; Lian was a criminal, yet Zhihuan lingered with him in tears—he ought to be struck from the rolls; in fact Lian had never passed through Macheng.
translations.idiomatic: It was alleged that when Lian was arrested he had passed through Macheng; Lian was a criminal, yet Zhihuan had lingered with him in tears—he ought to be struck from the rolls; in fact Lian had never passed through Macheng at all.

sentences.zh: 無何，逆黨梁克順誣以贓私，詔征贓。

translations.literal: Before long the partisan Liang Keshun falsely accused him of corruption; an edict ordered the recovery of illicit gains.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the partisan Liang Keshun falsely accused him of corruption, and an edict ordered the recovery of illicit gains.

sentences.zh: 之煥雖文士，負材武，善射，既廢，無所見。

translations.literal: Though Zhihuan was a literary man, he possessed martial talent, was skilled in archery, and once dismissed had no outlet for it.
translations.idiomatic: Though Zhihuan was a literary man, he possessed martial talent and was skilled in archery; once dismissed, he had no outlet for it.

sentences.zh: 所居縣，阻山多盜。

translations.literal: The county where he lived was mountainous and full of bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The county where he lived was cut off by mountains and full of bandits.

sentences.zh: 之煥無事，輒率健兒助吏捕，無脫者。

translations.literal: When he had nothing else to do, Zhihuan would lead stalwart youths to help the clerks capture them, and none escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he had nothing else to do, Zhihuan would lead stalwart youths to help the clerks capture them, and none escaped.

sentences.zh: 先是，甘肅兵變，其潰卒畏捕誅，往往亡命山谷間，為群盜，賊勢益張。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Gansu army mutinied, its scattered troops, fearing capture and execution, often fled into the mountain valleys and became bandit gangs, and the rebels grew ever stronger.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the Gansu army mutinied, its scattered troops, fearing capture and execution, often fled into the mountain valleys and became bandit gangs, and rebel strength grew ever greater.

sentences.zh: 至是，賊數萬來攻麻城，望見之煥部署，輒引去。

translations.literal: At this time tens of thousands of bandits came to attack Macheng; when they saw Zhihuan's dispositions they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: At this time tens of thousands of bandits came to attack Macheng; when they saw Zhihuan's dispositions they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 帝追敘甘肅前後功，復之煥官，蔭子，然終不召。

translations.literal: The emperor, reviewing earlier and later merit in Gansu, restored Zhihuan's office and granted hereditary privilege to his son, yet in the end never summoned him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, reviewing Zhihuan's earlier and later merit in Gansu, restored his office and granted hereditary privilege to his son, yet in the end never summoned him back.

sentences.zh: 明年病卒。

translations.literal: The next year he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he died of illness.

sentences.zh: 劉策，字範董，武定人。

translations.literal: Liu Ce, style Fandong, was a native of Wuding.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ce, whose style name was Fandong, came from Wuding.

sentences.zh: 萬歷二十九年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the twenty-ninth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the twenty-ninth year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 由保定新城知縣入為御史，疏劾太仆少卿徐兆魁，復力爭熊廷弼行勘及湯賓尹科場事。

translations.literal: From magistrate of Xincheng in Baoding he entered office as censor, memorialized to impeach Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Stud Xu Zhaokui, and again forcefully argued over Xiong Tingbi's field investigation and Tang Binyin’s examination scandal.
translations.idiomatic: From magistrate of Xincheng in Baoding he entered office as censor, memorialized to impeach Xu Zhaokui, vice minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud, and again forcefully argued over Xiong Tingbi's field investigation and Tang Binyin's examination scandal.

sentences.zh: 賓尹雖家居，遙執朝柄，嗾其黨逐攻者孫振基、王時熙。

translations.literal: Though Binyin lived at home, he held the reins of court power from afar and incited his faction to drive out his attackers Sun Zhenji and Wang Shixi.
translations.idiomatic: Though Binyin lived at home, he held the reins of court power from afar and incited his faction to drive out his attackers Sun Zhenji and Wang Shixi.

sentences.zh: 已而給事中劉文炳劾兩淮巡鹽御史徐縉芳，言策入葉向高幕，幹票擬；

translations.literal: Before long the supervising secretary Liu Wenbing impeached Xu Jinfang, the touring salt censor of the two Huai circuits, saying Ce had entered Ye Xianggao's staff and interfered in nomination slips;
translations.idiomatic: Before long the supervising secretary Liu Wenbing impeached Xu Jinfang, the touring salt censor of the two Huai circuits, saying that Ce had entered Ye Xianggao's staff and interfered in nomination slips;

sentences.zh: 策同官陳一元，向高姻親，顧權利。

translations.literal: Ce's colleague Chen Yiyuan was Xianggao's affinal relative and looked to power and profit.
translations.idiomatic: Ce's colleague Chen Yiyuan was Xianggao's affinal relative and looked to power and profit.

sentences.zh: 時策按宣、大，疏言：「文炳為湯賓尹死友，代韓敬反噬。

translations.literal: At the time Ce was touring Xuan and Da, and memorialized: "Wenbing is Binyin's sworn friend and acts for Han Jing in counterattack. Those who once exposed wrongdoing, such as Zhenji and Shixi—where are they now?
translations.idiomatic: At the time Ce was touring Xuan and Da and memorialized: "Wenbing is Binyin's sworn friend and acts for Han Jing in counterattack. Those who once exposed wrongdoing, such as Zhenji and Shixi—where are they now?

sentences.zh: 昔年發奸如振基、時熙輩，今皆安在？」

translations.literal: The men who once exposed wrongdoing, such as Zhenji and Shixi—where are they now?"
translations.idiomatic: Those who once exposed wrongdoing, such as Zhenji and Shixi—where are they now?"

sentences.zh: 向高亦以策無私交，為辨雪。

translations.literal: Xianggao also, because Ce had no private tie, cleared him.
translations.idiomatic: Xianggao also, because Ce had no private tie with him, spoke to clear him.

sentences.zh: 文炳、策屢疏相詆，南京御史吳良輔言：「文炳一疏而彈御史縉芳、一元、策及李若星，再疏而彈詞臣蔡毅中、焦竑及監司李維楨，他波及尚多。

translations.literal: Wenbing and Ce repeatedly memorialized against each other; the Nanjing censor Wu Liangfu said: "With one memorial Wenbing impeached the censors Jinfang, Yiyuan, Ce, and Li Ruoxing; with a second he impeached the academicians Cai Yizhong and Jiao Hong and the surveillance commissioner Li Weizhen, and many others were drawn in besides.
translations.idiomatic: Wenbing and Ce repeatedly memorialized against each other. The Nanjing censor Wu Liangfu said: "With one memorial Wenbing impeached the censors Jinfang, Yiyuan, Ce, and Li Ruoxing; with a second he impeached the academicians Cai Yizhong and Jiao Hong and the surveillance commissioner Li Weizhen, and many others were drawn in besides.

sentences.zh: 人才摧殘甚易，清品如策，雅望如竑，不免詆斥，天下寧有完人？」

translations.literal: Talent is very easily destroyed; men of pure character like Ce and of lofty reputation like Hong cannot escape vilification—can there be perfect men under heaven?"
translations.idiomatic: Talent is destroyed all too easily; men of pure character like Ce and of lofty reputation like Hong cannot escape vilification—can there be perfect men under heaven?"

sentences.zh: 策復詆文炳倚方從哲為冰山，茍一時富貴，不顧清議。

translations.literal: Ce again vilified Wenbing for relying on Fang Congzhe as an iceberg, grasping momentary wealth and honor without regard for public opinion.
translations.idiomatic: Ce again vilified Wenbing for relying on Fang Congzhe as an iceberg, grasping momentary wealth and honor without regard for public opinion.

sentences.zh: 一元論銓政，嘗譏切向高，時按江西，見文炳疏，憤甚，遂揭文炳陰事。

translations.literal: Yiyuan, discussing personnel administration, had once sharply criticized Xianggao; at the time he was touring Jiangxi, and when he saw Wenbing's memorial he was furious and exposed Wenbing's secret affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yiyuan, discussing personnel administration, had once sharply criticized Xianggao; at the time he was touring Jiangxi, and when he saw Wenbing's memorial he was furious and exposed Wenbing's secret affairs.

sentences.zh: 且曰：「向高行矣。

translations.literal: He also said: "Xianggao is leaving.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "Xianggao is leaving.

sentences.zh: 今秉政者從哲，文炳鄉人，奴顏婢膝，任好為之。」

translations.literal: Now the one holding power is Congzhe; Wenbing is his fellow townsman, fawning and servile, doing whatever he pleases."
translations.idiomatic: Now the one holding power is Congzhe; Wenbing is his fellow townsman, fawning and servile, doing whatever he pleases."

sentences.zh: 御史馬孟楨亦言：「敬關節實真，既斥兩侍郎、兩給諫謝之矣。

translations.literal: The censor Ma Mengzhen also said: "Jing's integrity was real; two vice ministers and two supervising secretaries have already been dismissed in his cause.
translations.idiomatic: The censor Ma Mengzhen also said: "Jing's integrity was real; two vice ministers and two supervising secretaries have already been dismissed in his cause.

sentences.zh: 乃伉直之劉策，攻擊不休，而同發奸之張篤敬復驅除將及，何太甚也！」

translations.literal: Yet the upright Liu Ce attacks without cease, and Zhang Dujing, who likewise exposed wrongdoing, is about to be driven out as well—how excessive!"
translations.idiomatic: Yet the upright Liu Ce attacks without cease, and Zhang Dujing, who likewise exposed wrongdoing, is about to be driven out as well—how excessive!"

sentences.zh: 疏入，帝皆不省。

translations.literal: When the memorials entered, the emperor paid no heed to any of them.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorials entered court, the emperor paid no heed to any of them.

sentences.zh: 策憤，謝病去。

translations.literal: Ce, furious, resigned on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Ce, furious, resigned on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 時攻兆魁、廷弼、賓尹輩者，黨人率指目為東林，以年例出之外。

translations.literal: At the time those who attacked Zhaokui, Tingbi, Binyin, and the like were generally pointed at by factionalists as Donglin men and, by seniority rule, sent out of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: At the time those who attacked Zhaokui, Tingbi, Binyin, and the like were generally pointed at by factionalists as Donglin men and, by seniority rule, sent out of the capital.

sentences.zh: 至四十六年秋，在朝者已無可逐，乃即家徙策為河南副使，策辭疾不赴。

translations.literal: By autumn of the forty-sixth year there was no one left in court to drive out; they then transferred Ce from his home to vice commissioner of Henan, and Ce declined on grounds of illness and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: By autumn of the forty-sixth year there was no one left in court to drive out; they then transferred Ce from his home to vice commissioner of Henan, and Ce declined on grounds of illness and did not go.

sentences.zh: 天啟元年春，起天津兵備。

translations.literal: In the spring of the first year of Tianqi he was raised to defend military affairs at Tianjin.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the first year of Tianqi he was raised to defend military affairs at Tianjin.

sentences.zh: 擢右僉都御史，巡撫山西。

translations.literal: He was promoted to right vice censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to right vice censor-in-chief and appointed grand coordinator of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 召拜兵部右侍郎，協理戎政。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed vice minister of War, assisting in military administration.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned and appointed vice minister of War, assisting in military administration.

sentences.zh: 五年冬，黨人劾策為東林遺奸，遂削籍。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fifth year factionalists impeached Ce as a surviving Donglin villain, and he was struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the fifth year factionalists impeached Ce as a surviving Donglin villain, and he was struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 崇禎二年夏，起故官，兼右僉都御史，總理薊、遼、保定軍務。

translations.literal: In the summer of the second year of Chongzhen he was restored to his former office, also serving as right vice censor-in-chief to oversee military affairs in Ji, Liao, and Baoding.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the second year of Chongzhen he was restored to his former office and also made right vice censor-in-chief to oversee military affairs in Ji, Liao, and Baoding.

sentences.zh: 大清兵由大安口入內地，策不能禦，被劾。

translations.literal: The Great Qing army entered the interior through Daankou; Ce could not defend against them and was impeached.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Qing army entered the interior through Daankou; Ce could not defend against them and was impeached.

sentences.zh: 祖大壽東潰，策偕孫承宗招使還。

translations.literal: Zu Dashou fled east in collapse; Ce together with Sun Chengzong summoned and brought him back.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Dashou fled east in collapse; Ce together with Sun Chengzong summoned him and brought him back.

sentences.zh: 明年正月與總兵張士顯並逮，論死，棄市。

translations.literal: In the first month of the next year he and the regional commander Zhang Shixian were arrested together, sentenced to death, and executed in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the next year he and the regional commander Zhang Shixian were arrested together, sentenced to death, and executed in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 縉芳，晉江人。

translations.literal: Jinfang was a native of Jinjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Jinfang was a native of Jinjiang.

sentences.zh: 為御史，首為顧憲成請謚，劾天津稅監馬堂九大罪，有敢言名。

translations.literal: As censor he was the first to request a posthumous title for Gu Xiancheng and impeached the Tianjin tax commissioner Ma Tang on nine great crimes, earning a reputation for daring speech.
translations.idiomatic: As censor he was the first to request a posthumous title for Gu Xiancheng and impeached the Tianjin tax commissioner Ma Tang on nine great crimes, earning a reputation for daring speech.

sentences.zh: 巡兩淮，頗通賓客賂遺，被劾，坐贓。

translations.literal: Touring the two Huai circuits he widely entertained guests and accepted gifts, was impeached, and convicted of corruption.
translations.idiomatic: While touring the two Huai circuits he widely entertained guests and accepted gifts, was impeached, and convicted of corruption.

sentences.zh: 天啟中，遣戍。

translations.literal: In the Tianqi period he was sent into exile.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianqi period he was sent into exile.

sentences.zh: 一元，侯官人。

translations.literal: Yiyuan was a native of Houguan.
translations.idiomatic: Yiyuan was a native of Houguan.

sentences.zh: 在江西，振饑有法。

translations.literal: In Jiangxi he relieved famine with effective methods.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiangxi he relieved famine with effective methods.

sentences.zh: 移疾去。

translations.literal: He resigned on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，起歷應天府丞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianqi he was raised and served in succession as vice prefect of Yingtian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianqi he was raised and served in succession as vice prefect of Yingtian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 御史余文縉劾向高，及一元，遂落職。

translations.literal: The censor Yu Wenjin impeached Xianggao and also Yiyuan, and he was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: The censor Yu Wenjin impeached Xianggao and also Yiyuan, and Yiyuan was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 崇禎初，復官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chongzhen his office was restored.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Chongzhen his office was restored.

sentences.zh: 溫體仁柄國，惡其附東林，而以為己門生也，引嫌不召。

translations.literal: When Wen Tiren held power he hated Yiyuan for siding with the Donglin and, because he regarded him as his own student, declined to summon him on grounds of personal connection.
translations.idiomatic: When Wen Tiren held power he hated Yiyuan for siding with the Donglin and, because he regarded him as his own student, declined to summon him on grounds of personal connection.

sentences.zh: 卒於家。

translations.literal: He died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home.

sentences.zh: 李若星，字紫垣，息縣人。

translations.literal: Li Ruoxing, style Ziyuan, was a native of Xi County.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ruoxing, whose style name was Ziyuan, came from Xi County.

sentences.zh: 萬歷三十二年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the thirty-second year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the thirty-second year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 歷知棗強、真定。

translations.literal: He served in succession as magistrate of Zaoqiang and Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: He served in succession as magistrate of Zaoqiang and Zhending.

sentences.zh: 擢御史，首劾南京兵部尚書黃克纘。

translations.literal: He was promoted to censor and was the first to impeach Huang Kezuan, minister of War at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to censor and was the first to impeach Huang Kezuan, minister of War at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 巡視庫藏，陳蠹國病商四弊，請得稽十庫出納，以杜侵漁，不報。

translations.literal: Inspecting the treasuries, he set forth four abuses that harmed the state and injured merchants, and asked to audit the receipts and disbursements of the ten treasuries to stop embezzlement; no reply came.
translations.idiomatic: While inspecting the treasuries he set forth four abuses that harmed the state and injured merchants, and asked to audit the receipts and disbursements of the ten treasuries to stop embezzlement; no reply came.

sentences.zh: 巡按山西，請撤稅使。

translations.literal: Touring Shanxi, he asked that the tax commissioners be withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: While touring Shanxi he asked that the tax commissioners be withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 因再劾克纘為沈一貫私人、湯賓尹死友，宜罷，不從。

translations.literal: He therefore again impeached Kezuan as a private man of Shen Yiguan and a sworn friend of Tang Binyin, and said he ought to be dismissed; the court did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore again impeached Kezuan as a private man of Shen Yiguan and a sworn friend of Tang Binyin and said he ought to be dismissed; the court did not agree.

sentences.zh: 還朝，出為福建右參議，移疾歸。

translations.literal: Returning to court, he went out as right vice commissioner of Fujian and resigned on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Returning to court, he went out as right vice commissioner of Fujian and resigned on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，起官陜西，召為尚寶少卿，再遷大理右少卿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianqi he was raised to office in Shaanxi, summoned as vice minister of the Court of Imperial Seals, and again promoted to right vice minister of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianqi he was raised to office in Shaanxi, summoned as vice minister of the Court of Imperial Seals, and again promoted to right vice minister of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 三年春，以右僉都御史巡撫甘肅。

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year he was made right vice censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the third year he was made right vice censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Gansu.

sentences.zh: 陛辭，發魏忠賢、客氏之奸。

translations.literal: At his audience of leave he exposed the villainy of Wei Zhongxian and Lady Ke.
translations.idiomatic: At his audience of leave he exposed the villainy of Wei Zhongxian and Lady Ke.

sentences.zh: 明年，遣將丁孟科、官維賢擊河套松山諸部鎮番，斬首二百四十余級。

translations.literal: The next year he sent the generals Ding Mengke and Guan Weixian to strike the Ordos and Songshan tribes at Zhenfan, taking more than two hundred forty heads.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he sent the generals Ding Mengke and Guan Weixian to strike the Ordos and Songshan tribes at Zhenfan, taking more than two hundred forty heads.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，未敘，有傳若星將起義兵清君側之惡者。

translations.literal: When victory was reported, before rewards were granted there was a rumor that Ruoxing would raise an army of righteousness to purge the evil at the ruler's side.
translations.idiomatic: When victory was reported, before rewards were granted there was a rumor that Ruoxing would raise an army of righteousness to purge the evil at the ruler's side.

sentences.zh: 忠賢聞之，即令許顯純入之汪文言獄詞，誣其賄趙南星，得節鉞。

translations.literal: When Zhongxian heard it, he immediately had Xu Xianchun insert it into the case testimony of Wang Wenyan, falsely accusing him of bribing Zhao Nanxing to obtain a command baton.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongxian heard it, he immediately had Xu Xianchun insert it into the case testimony of Wang Wenyan, falsely accusing Ruoxing of bribing Zhao Nanxing to obtain a command baton.

sentences.zh: 五年三月遂除若星名，下河南撫按提問。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fifth year Ruoxing was then dismissed by name and sent down to the Henan grand coordinator and touring censor for interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the fifth year Ruoxing was formally dismissed and handed over to the Henan grand coordinator and touring censor for interrogation.

sentences.zh: 明年，獄上，杖之百，戍廉州。

translations.literal: The next year, when the case was submitted, he was beaten one hundred strokes and banished to Lianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, when the case was concluded, he received one hundred strokes of the rod and was exiled to Lianzhou.

sentences.zh: 福王時，解職。

translations.literal: During the reign of the Prince of Fu he was released from office.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Prince of Fu he was restored and relieved of his former sentence.

sentences.zh: 以鄉邑殘破，寓居貴州。

translations.literal: Because his native district lay in ruins, he took up residence in Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: With his home region devastated by war, he made his home in Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 桂王遷武岡，召為吏部尚書。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Gui moved to Wugang, Ruoxing was summoned as minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Gui withdrew to Wugang, Ruoxing was called to serve as minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 未赴，遭亂，死於兵。

translations.literal: Before he could take up the post he was caught in the turmoil and died in the fighting.
translations.idiomatic: He never reached his post; caught in the chaos of war, he perished in battle.

sentences.zh: 耿如杞，字楚材，館陶人。

translations.literal: Geng Ruqi, style Chucai, was a native of Guantao.
translations.idiomatic: Geng Ruqi, whose style name was Chucai, came from Guantao.

sentences.zh: 萬歷四十四年進士。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year of Wanli he passed the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: He became a metropolitan graduate in the forty-fourth year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 除戶部主事。

translations.literal: He was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He received appointment as a secretary in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，以才歷職方郎中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianqi, on account of his talent he rose through the Bureau of Military Appointments as a director.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Tianqi reign his ability won him appointment as a director in the Bureau of Military Appointments.

sentences.zh: 軍書旁午，日應數十事。

translations.literal: Military dispatches came in crisscrossing waves, and he answered dozens of matters each day.
translations.idiomatic: Military dispatches poured in from every quarter, and he disposed of dozens of cases every day.

sentences.zh: 出為陜西參議，遷遵化兵備副使。

translations.literal: He went out as a Shaanxi vice commissioner and was promoted to vice commissioner for military defense at Zunhua.
translations.idiomatic: He left the capital as a Shaanxi vice commissioner and was promoted to vice commissioner for military defense at Zunhua.

sentences.zh: 當是時，逆奄竊柄，諂子無所不至，至建祠祝禧。

translations.literal: At that time the rebellious eunuch usurped power, and flatterers stopped at nothing, even building temples to offer blessings for his long life.
translations.idiomatic: In those days the eunuch faction held the reins of power, and sycophants went to every extreme, even erecting temples to pray for his longevity.

sentences.zh: 巡撫劉詔懸忠賢畫像於喜峰行署，率文武將吏五拜三稽首，呼九千歲。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Liu Zhao hung Zhongxian's portrait in his field headquarters at Xifeng, led civil and military officers in five bows and three full prostrations, and shouted "Nine thousand years!"
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Liu Zhao displayed Zhongxian's portrait at his field headquarters in Xifeng, led civil and military officers in five bows and three full prostrations, and cried, "Nine thousand years!"

sentences.zh: 如杞見其像，冕旒也，半揖而出。

translations.literal: When Ruqi saw the portrait, he saw it bore the imperial crown and regalia; he gave only a half bow and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Ruqi saw that the portrait bore the imperial crown and regalia; he offered only a half bow and walked out.

sentences.zh: 忠賢令詔劾之，逮下詔獄，坐贓六千三百，論死。

translations.literal: Zhongxian ordered Zhao to impeach him; Ruqi was seized and sent to the imperial prison, convicted of six thousand three hundred in embezzlement, and sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxian had Zhao impeach him. Ruqi was arrested and thrown into the imperial prison, convicted on a charge of embezzling six thousand three hundred taels, and condemned to death.

sentences.zh: 時又有胡士容者，薊州參議也，數忤其鄉官崔呈秀，呈秀銜之。

translations.literal: At the time there was also a Hu Shirong, a vice commissioner of Jizhou, who repeatedly crossed his fellow townsman Cui Chengxiu; Chengxiu bore a grudge against him.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Hu Shirong, a Jizhou vice commissioner, who repeatedly defied his fellow townsman Cui Chengxiu, and Chengxiu nursed a deep grievance against him.

sentences.zh: 將為忠賢建祠，士容又不奉命。

translations.literal: When a temple was to be built for Zhongxian, Shirong again refused to obey the order.
translations.idiomatic: When officials planned a temple for Zhongxian, Shirong once again refused to comply.

sentences.zh: 及士容遷江西副使，道通州，遂誣以多乘驛馬，侵盜倉儲，捕下詔獄掠治，坐贓七千，論死。

translations.literal: When Shirong was transferred to be a Jiangxi vice commissioner and passed through Tongzhou, he was falsely accused of taking too many relay horses and plundering the granaries; he was seized, sent to the imperial prison, and tortured until convicted of seven thousand in embezzlement and sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: After Shirong was promoted to Jiangxi vice commissioner and passed through Tongzhou, he was framed for abusing relay horses and looting the granaries, seized and thrown into the imperial prison, tortured until convicted of embezzling seven thousand taels, and condemned to death.

sentences.zh: 插漢虎墩兔據順義王地，為邊患，戰款無定策。

translations.literal: Chaahan Tudun occupied the territory of the Prince of Shunyang and became a border menace; policy wavered between war and negotiation with no settled plan.
translations.idiomatic: Chaahan Tudun held the Prince of Shunyang's territory and plagued the frontier, while court policy lurched between fighting and negotiating without a fixed course.

sentences.zh: 如杞言守邊為上，修塞垣，繕戰壘，鏟山塹谷，事有緒矣。

translations.literal: Ruqi argued that holding the border was paramount: repair the frontier walls, mend the battle ramparts, cut through mountains and dig valleys—and the work was beginning to take shape.
translations.idiomatic: Ruqi urged that defense of the frontier came first: repair the walls, rebuild the fortifications, cut passes through the mountains and dig trenches in the valleys—and the work was finally gaining momentum.

sentences.zh: 二年，京師戒嚴，如杞率總兵官張鴻功以卒五千人赴援，先至京師。

translations.literal: In the second year, when the capital was placed under emergency guard, Ruqi led the regional commander Zhang Honggong with five thousand troops to the relief of the capital and arrived first.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, when Beijing was placed on war footing, Ruqi marched to the capital at the head of five thousand men under Regional Commander Zhang Honggong and was the first to arrive.

sentences.zh: 軍令，卒至之明日，汛地既定，而後乃給餉。

translations.literal: By military regulation, on the day after troops arrived their garrison station had first to be fixed, and only then would rations be issued.
translations.idiomatic: Army regulations required that rations be issued only after a unit's garrison station had been fixed on the day following its arrival.

sentences.zh: 如杞兵既至，兵部令守通州，明日調昌平，又明日調良鄉，汛地累更，軍三日不得餉，乃噪而大掠。

translations.literal: Once Ruqi's troops had arrived, the Ministry of War ordered them to guard Tongzhou; the next day they were shifted to Changping, and the day after that to Liangxiang. Their garrison stations were changed again and again; for three days the army received no rations, and the men clamored and looted on a great scale.
translations.idiomatic: Ruqi's men had barely arrived when the Ministry of War ordered them to Tongzhou, then to Changping the next day, and to Liangxiang the day after that. Station after station was changed; for three days the troops received no pay, and they mutinied and plundered wildly.

sentences.zh: 帝聞之，大怒，詔逮如杞、鴻功，廷臣莫敢救者。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of it he was furious and ordered Ruqi and Honggong arrested; no court minister dared plead for them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was enraged when he heard of it and ordered Ruqi and Honggong seized; not one minister at court dared speak in their defense.

sentences.zh: 四年竟斬西市。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was at last beheaded at the West Market.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was finally executed at the West Market.

sentences.zh: 方如杞之為職方郎也，與主事鹿善繼黨張鶴鳴，排熊廷弼而庇王化貞，疆事由是大壞，及是得罪。

translations.literal: When Ruqi had served as a Bureau of Military Appointments director, he had joined the chief clerk Lu Shanji in siding with Zhang Heming, had pushed out Xiong Tingbi and shielded Wang Huazhen, and frontier affairs were thereby greatly ruined; now he met with punishment.
translations.idiomatic: In his days as a Bureau of Military Appointments director, Ruqi had banded with Chief Clerk Lu Shanji behind Zhang Heming, had driven out Xiong Tingbi and protected Wang Huazhen, and the frontier had suffered grievously for it; now he paid the price.

sentences.zh: 士容既釋出獄，二年除陜西副使，進右參政，卒於官。

translations.literal: After Shirong was released from prison, in the second year he was appointed Shaanxi vice commissioner, promoted to right vice commissioner, and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Once released from prison, Shirong was appointed Shaanxi vice commissioner in the second year, rose to right vice commissioner, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 士容初令長洲，捕豪惡，築婁江石塘，有政聲。

translations.literal: Shirong had first served as magistrate of Changzhou, where he arrested powerful ruffians and built the Loujiang stone embankment, winning a reputation for good governance.
translations.idiomatic: Shirong had first served as magistrate of Changzhou, where he seized local bullies, built the Loujiang stone dike, and earned a name for effective rule.

sentences.zh: 福王時，贈如杞右僉都御史。

translations.literal: During the reign of the Prince of Fu, Ruqi was posthumously enfeoffed as right vice censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Prince of Fu, Ruqi was posthumously honored as right vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 子章光，進士，尚寶卿。

translations.literal: His son Zhangguang became a metropolitan graduate and served as court of imperial seals minister.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhangguang passed the metropolitan examination and rose to court of imperial seals minister.

sentences.zh: 士容，字仁常，廣濟人。

translations.literal: Shirong, style Renchang, was a native of Guangji.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Shirong, whose style name was Renchang, came from Guangji.

sentences.zh: 遷工科右給事中。

translations.literal: Jizu was transferred to right supervising secretary in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Jizu was promoted to right supervising secretary in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 三年，巡視京城十六門濠塹，疏列八事，劾監督主事方應明曠職。

translations.literal: In the third year Jizu inspected the moats and ramparts of the capital's sixteen gates, memorialized eight matters in a memorial, and impeached Supervising Secretary Fang Yingming for neglect of duty.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he inspected the moats and walls of the capital's sixteen gates, set forth eight recommendations in a memorial, and impeached Supervising Secretary Fang Yingming for dereliction of duty.

sentences.zh: 帝杖斥應明。

translations.literal: The emperor had Yingming beaten and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had Yingming flogged and driven from office.

sentences.zh: 外城庳薄，議加高厚，繼祖言時絀難舉贏而止。

translations.literal: The outer walls were low and thin; there was talk of raising and thickening them, but Jizu said the times were straitened and that to attempt more would only overreach and fail, and the plan was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The outer walls were low and flimsy, and officials debated raising and thickening them, but Jizu argued that resources were too scarce to take on more and the proposal was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 再遷吏科都給事中，疏陳時事十大弊。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to chief supervising secretary of the Ministry of Personnel and memorialized ten great abuses of the day.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to chief supervising secretary of the Ministry of Personnel and submitted a memorial on ten grave abuses of the age.

sentences.zh: 憂歸。

translations.literal: He returned home on account of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned and returned home to observe mourning.

sentences.zh: 八年起故官，上言：「六部之政筦於尚書，諸司之務握之正郎，而侍郎及副郎、主事止陪列畫題，政事安得不廢？

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was restored to his former post and memorialized: "The administration of the Six Ministries rests with the ministers, and the business of each bureau lies in the hands of the chief directors; yet vice ministers, associate directors, and chief clerks do nothing but sit in attendance and affix their signatures—how can government not fall into ruin?
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was restored to office and submitted a memorial: "The Six Ministries are governed by their ministers, and each bureau's affairs should be handled by its chief directors; yet vice ministers, associate directors, and chief clerks do nothing but sit in attendance and sign their names—how can government fail to collapse?

sentences.zh: 督撫諸臣獲罪者接踵，初皆由會推。

translations.literal: Grand coordinators and governors who were punished came one after another, and at first all had been chosen through collaborative nomination.
translations.idiomatic: Grand coordinators and governors who met punishment fell one after another, and all had originally been chosen through the collaborative nomination process.

sentences.zh: 然會推但六科掌篆者為主，卿貳、臺臣罕至。

translations.literal: Yet in collaborative nomination only the heads of the Six Offices of Scrutiny took the lead; vice ministers and censorial officials rarely attended.
translations.idiomatic: Yet collaborative nomination was dominated by the heads of the Six Offices of Scrutiny, while vice ministers and censorial officials seldom appeared.

sentences.zh: 且九卿、臺諫止選郎傳語，有唯諾，無翻異，何名會推？」

translations.literal: Moreover, the nine ministers and censorial remonstrators merely had a selection clerk relay the words; there was assent but no dissent—what could this be called collaborative nomination?
translations.idiomatic: Worse, the nine ministers and censorial remonstrators heard only a selection clerk relay the names; they nodded assent but never raised objection—what sort of collaborative nomination was this?

sentences.zh: 帝稱善。

translations.literal: The emperor praised the proposal.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved and praised the memorial.

sentences.zh: 尋擢太常少卿，以右僉都御史巡撫山東。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and appointed grand coordinator of Shandong with the rank of right vice censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and sent out as grand coordinator of Shandong with the rank of right vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 分兵扼境上，河南賊不敢窺青、濟。

translations.literal: He divided his troops to hold the border, and the bandits of Henan did not dare cast their eyes toward Qing and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: He deployed troops to block the frontier, and Henan bandits did not dare threaten Qingzhou and Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 劾故撫李懋芳侵軍餉二萬有奇，被旨嘉獎。

translations.literal: He impeached the former grand coordinator Li Maofang for embezzling more than twenty thousand in military rations and received an imperial commendation.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached the former grand coordinator Li Maofang for embezzling more than twenty thousand taels in military rations and was rewarded with an imperial commendation.

sentences.zh: 十一年，畿輔戒嚴，命繼祖移駐德州。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, when the capital region was placed under emergency guard, Jizu was ordered to move his headquarters to Dezhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, when the capital region went on war footing, Jizu was ordered to shift his headquarters to Dezhou.

sentences.zh: 時標下卒僅三千，而奉本兵楊嗣昌令，五旬三更調。

translations.literal: At the time the troops under his banner numbered only three thousand, yet he obeyed the orders of the minister of War Yang Sichang and was reassigned every fifteen days.
translations.idiomatic: He had barely three thousand men under his command, yet obeying Minister of War Yang Sichang's orders he was reassigned every fortnight.

sentences.zh: 後令專防德州，濟南由此空虛。

translations.literal: Later he was ordered to defend Dezhou exclusively, and Jinan was thereby left empty.
translations.idiomatic: He was later ordered to concentrate on Dezhou alone, leaving Jinan dangerously undefended.

sentences.zh: 繼祖屢請敕諸將劉澤清、倪寵等赴援，皆逗遛不進。

translations.literal: Jizu repeatedly asked that imperial orders be sent to the generals Liu Zeqing, Ni Chong, and others to hurry to the relief, but they all lingered and would not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Jizu repeatedly petitioned for imperial orders dispatching Generals Liu Zeqing, Ni Chong, and others to his aid, but they all stalled and refused to march.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，大清兵克濟南，執德王。

translations.literal: In the first month of the following year the Great Qing army took Jinan and captured the Prince of De.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the following year Qing forces captured Jinan and seized the Prince of De.

sentences.zh: 繼祖一人不能兼顧，言官交章劾繼祖，繼祖咎嗣昌，且曰：「臣兵少力弱，不敢居守德之功，不敢不分失濟之罪。

translations.literal: Jizu alone could not attend to everything; censorial officials submitted memorial after memorial impeaching him. Jizu blamed Sichang and said: "My troops are few and my strength weak; I dare not claim credit for holding Dezhou, nor dare I shirk blame for losing Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: Jizu could not be everywhere at once; remonstrating officials flooded the court with impeachments. Jizu blamed Sichang and declared: "My force is too small and too weak; I dare not claim credit for holding Dezhou, nor can I escape blame for the fall of Jinan.

sentences.zh: 請以爵祿還朝廷，以骸骨還父母。」

translations.literal: I ask to return my titles and stipends to the court and my bones to my parents.
translations.idiomatic: I beg to surrender my rank and emoluments to the throne and my worn body to my parents.

sentences.zh: 帝不從，逮下獄，棄市。

translations.literal: The emperor did not agree; Jizu was seized and thrown into prison and executed in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused. Jizu was arrested, imprisoned, and executed in the public marketplace.

sentences.zh: 終崇禎世，巡撫被戮者十有一人：薊鎮王應豸，山西耿如杞，宣府李養沖，登萊孫元化，大同張翼明，順天陳祖苞，保定張其平，山東顏繼祖，四川邵捷春，永平馬成名，順天潘永圖，而河南李仙風被逮自縊，不與焉。

translations.literal: Throughout the Chongzhen reign eleven grand coordinators were put to death: Wang Yingbi of Jizhou, Geng Ruqi of Shanxi, Li Yangchong of Xuanfu, Sun Yuanhua of Deng-Lai, Zhang Yiming of Datong, Chen Zubao of Shuntian, Zhang Qiping of Baoding, Yan Jizu of Shandong, Shao Jiechun of Sichuan, Ma Chengming of Yongping, and Pan Yongtu of Shuntian; Li Xianfeng of Henan was arrested and hanged himself and is not counted among them.
translations.idiomatic: Through the entire Chongzhen reign eleven grand coordinators were executed: Wang Yingbi of Jizhou, Geng Ruqi of Shanxi, Li Yangchong of Xuanfu, Sun Yuanhua of Deng-Lai, Zhang Yiming of Datong, Chen Zubao of Shuntian, Zhang Qiping of Baoding, Yan Jizu of Shandong, Shao Jiechun of Sichuan, Ma Chengming of Yongping, and Pan Yongtu of Shuntian. Li Xianfeng of Henan was arrested and took his own life and is not included in the count.

sentences.zh: 王應豸，掖縣人。

translations.literal: Wang Yingbi was a native of Ye County.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yingbi came from Ye County.

sentences.zh: 為戶部主事，諂魏忠賢，甫三歲，驟至巡撫，加右都御史。

translations.literal: As a secretary in the Ministry of Revenue he flattered Wei Zhongxian; in only three years he was suddenly made grand coordinator and promoted to right censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: While serving as a Ministry of Revenue secretary he fawned on Wei Zhongxian, and in a mere three years was abruptly elevated to grand coordinator and right censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 崇禎二年春，薊卒索餉，噪而甲，參政徐從治諭散其眾。

translations.literal: In the spring of the second year of Chongzhen the troops at Jizhou demanded pay, clamored, and took up arms; Vice Commissioner Xu Congzhi admonished them and dispersed the crowd.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Chongzhen 2 the Jizhou garrison demanded back pay, mutinied, and seized their weapons; Vice Commissioner Xu Congzhi reasoned with them and broke up the crowd.

sentences.zh: 應豸置毒飯中，欲誘而盡殺之，諸軍復大亂。

translations.literal: Yingbi put poison in the food, intending to lure them and kill them all; the army again fell into great disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Yingbi laced the rations with poison, hoping to lure the men in and slaughter them wholesale; the troops erupted in chaos once more.

sentences.zh: 帝命巡按方大任廉得其克餉狀，論死。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Touring Censor Fang Daren to investigate impartially and establish his withholding of pay; he was sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Touring Censor Fang Daren to investigate and confirmed that he had withheld pay; Yingbi was condemned to death.

sentences.zh: 李養沖，永年人。

translations.literal: Li Yangchong was a native of Yongnian.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yangchong came from Yongnian.

sentences.zh: 歷兵部右侍郎，巡撫宣府，崇禎二年既謝事，御史吳玉劾其侵盜撫賞銀七萬，及冒功匿敗諸狀。

translations.literal: He rose to vice minister of the Ministry of War and served as grand coordinator of Xuanfu; in the second year of Chongzhen, after he had already left office, Censor Wu Yu impeached him for embezzling seventy thousand taels in frontier reward silver and for claiming merit while concealing defeats.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to vice minister of the Ministry of War and served as grand coordinator of Xuanfu. In Chongzhen 2, after he had already retired, Censor Wu Yu impeached him for embezzling seventy thousand taels in frontier reward funds and for claiming victories while hiding defeats.

sentences.zh: 論死，斃於獄。

translations.literal: He was sentenced to death and died in prison.
translations.idiomatic: He was condemned to death and died in prison.

sentences.zh: 張翼明，永城人。

translations.literal: Zhang Yiming was a native of Yongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yiming came from Yongcheng.

sentences.zh: 以兵部右侍郎巡撫大同。

translations.literal: As vice minister of the Ministry of War he served as grand coordinator of Datong.
translations.idiomatic: He served as grand coordinator of Datong in the capacity of vice minister of the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 崇禎元年，插漢虎墩兔入犯，殺掠萬計。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongzhen, Chaahan Tudun invaded and killed and plundered by the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen 1 Chaahan Tudun raided across the border, killing and looting on a scale of tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 翼明及總兵官渠家楨不能禦，並坐死。

translations.literal: Yiming and Regional Commander Qu Jiazhen could not repel him; both were condemned to death.
translations.idiomatic: Yiming and Regional Commander Qu Jiazhen failed to drive him off; both were sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 陳祖苞，海寧人。

translations.literal: Chen Zubao was a native of Haining.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zubao came from Haining.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十年，以右副都御史巡撫順天，明年坐失事系獄，飲鴆卒。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Chongzhen he was made grand coordinator of Shuntian as right vice censor-in-chief; the next year, convicted of dereliction, he was imprisoned and died by drinking poison.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen 10 he was appointed grand coordinator of Shuntian with the rank of right vice censor-in-chief; the following year, convicted of failure in office, he was imprisoned and took poison.

sentences.zh: 帝怒祖苞漏刑，錮其子編修之遴，永不敘。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry that Zubao had evaded execution; he barred his son, Compiler Zhi Lin, from office forever.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was enraged that Zubao had cheated the executioner; he permanently barred his son, Compiler Zhi Lin, from official service.

sentences.zh: 張其平，偃師人。

translations.literal: Zhang Qiping was a native of Yanshi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Qiping came from Yanshi.

sentences.zh: 歷右僉都御史，巡撫保定。

translations.literal: He rose to right vice censor-in-chief and served as grand coordinator of Baoding.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to right vice censor-in-chief and served as grand coordinator of Baoding.

sentences.zh: 十一年冬，坐屬邑失亡多，與繼祖駢死西市。

translations.literal: In the winter of the eleventh year, convicted because many subordinate districts had fallen, he was executed at the West Market together with Jizu.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the eleventh year, convicted because too many counties under his jurisdiction had been lost, he was executed at the West Market alongside Jizu.

sentences.zh: 馬成名，溧陽人。

translations.literal: Ma Chengming was a native of Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Chengming came from Liyang.

sentences.zh: 潘永圖，金壇人，與成名為姻婭。

translations.literal: Pan Yongtu was a native of Jintan and was related to Chengming by marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Yongtu came from Jintan and was connected to Chengming by marriage.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十四年冬，成名以右僉都御史巡撫永平。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fourteenth year of Chongzhen, Chengming was made grand coordinator of Yongping as right vice censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of Chongzhen 14 Chengming was appointed grand coordinator of Yongping with the rank of right vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 永圖亦起昌平兵備僉事，未浹歲，至巡撫。

translations.literal: Yongtu also rose from vice commissioner for military defense at Changping; within less than a year he reached grand coordinator.
translations.idiomatic: Yongtu likewise rose from vice commissioner for military defense at Changping and within a year had become grand coordinator.

sentences.zh: 畿輔被兵，成名、永圖並以失機，十六年斬西市。

translations.literal: When the capital region suffered invasion, Chengming and Yongtu were both convicted of missing their moment; in the sixteenth year they were beheaded at the West Market.
translations.idiomatic: When war swept the capital region, Chengming and Yongtu were both condemned for failing to seize the moment; in the sixteenth year they were executed at the West Market.

sentences.zh: 余自有傳。

translations.literal: Yu has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Dacheng has his own biography elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 李繼貞，字征尹，太倉州人。

translations.literal: Li Jizhen, style Zhengyin, was a native of Taicang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jizhen, whose style name was Zhengyin, came from Taicang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 萬歷四十一年進士。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year of Wanli he passed the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: He became a metropolitan graduate in the forty-first year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 除大名推官，歷遷兵部職方主事。

translations.literal: He was appointed investigating censor of Daming and rose through the posts to chief clerk in the Bureau of Military Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed investigating censor of Daming and rose through the ranks to chief clerk in the Bureau of Military Appointments.

sentences.zh: 天啟四年秋，典試山東，坐試錄刺魏忠賢，降級，已而削籍。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the fourth year of Tianqi, while serving as chief examiner in Shandong, he was demoted because the examination record satirized Wei Zhongxian, and later was struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of Tianqi 4, while chief examiner in Shandong, he was demoted because the examination record mocked Wei Zhongxian and was later removed from the register of officials.

sentences.zh: 繼貞為人強項，在事清執，請謁不得行。

translations.literal: Jizhen was a man of stern character; in office he was upright and uncompromising, and requests through personal connections could not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: Jizhen was unyielding by nature; in office he held to principle without compromise, and no favor could move him.

sentences.zh: 大學士周延儒，繼貞同年生，屬總兵官於繼貞。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Zhou Yanru, a fellow graduate of the same year, asked Jizhen to appoint a regional commander for him.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Zhou Yanru, who had passed the examinations the same year, asked Jizhen to place a regional commander on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 繼貞瞠目謝曰：「我不奉命，必獲罪。

translations.literal: Jizhen stared wide-eyed and declined, saying: "If I obey this order, I am sure to be punished.
translations.idiomatic: Jizhen fixed him with a stare and refused, saying, "If I do as you ask, I am sure to end up in prison.

sentences.zh: 刑部獄甚寬，可容繼貞也。」

translations.literal: The prison of the Ministry of Punishments is very spacious; it can hold Jizhen as well.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Punishments runs a very spacious prison—it has room enough for me.

sentences.zh: 延儒銜之。

translations.literal: Yanru bore a grudge against him.
translations.idiomatic: Yanru never forgave the slight.

sentences.zh: 已，加尚寶寺卿。

translations.literal: Later he was promoted to court of imperial seals minister.
translations.idiomatic: He was subsequently promoted to court of imperial seals minister.

sentences.zh: 當遷，帝輒令久任。

translations.literal: Whenever he was due for transfer, the emperor repeatedly ordered him to remain long in his post.
translations.idiomatic: Each time a transfer came due, the emperor ordered him to remain in office.

sentences.zh: 田貴妃父弘遇以坐門功求優敘不獲，屢疏詆繼貞，帝不聽。

translations.literal: Tian Guifei's father Hongyu, seeking preferential promotion for meritorious service at the palace gate and failing to obtain it, repeatedly memorialized to slander Jizhen, but the emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Hongyu, father of Consort Tian, sought preferential promotion for his service at the palace gate; denied, he repeatedly memorialized to vilify Jizhen, but the emperor paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 中官曹化淳欲用私人為把總，繼貞不可；

translations.literal: The eunuch Cao Huachun wished to install a protégé as a company commander, and Jizhen would not agree;
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Cao Huachun wanted to install a protégé as a company commander, and Jizhen refused;

sentences.zh: 乃囑戎政尚書陸完學言於尚書張鳳翼以命繼貞，繼貞亦不可，鳳翼排繼貞議而用之。

translations.literal: Huachun then asked Military Affairs Minister Lu Wanxue to speak to Minister Zhang Fengyi so that the order might be sent to Jizhen, but Jizhen again refused; Fengyi set aside Jizhen's objection and carried out the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Huachun then had Military Affairs Minister Lu Wanxue speak to Minister Zhang Fengyi to pass down the order, but Jizhen refused again; Fengyi overruled him and made the appointment.

sentences.zh: 化淳怒，與弘遇日伺其隙，讒之帝，坐小誤，貶三秩。

translations.literal: Huachun was angry; he and Hongyu watched daily for an opening and slandered Jizhen to the emperor; on a minor fault he was demoted three ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Huachun was furious; he and Hongyu watched daily for a chance to denounce Jizhen to the emperor, and on a trifling error he was demoted three ranks.

sentences.zh: 會敘甘肅功，繼貞請起用故巡撫梅之煥，帝遂發怒，削繼貞籍。

translations.literal: When Gansu achievements were being rewarded, Jizhen asked that the former grand coordinator Mei Zhihuan be restored to office; the emperor thereupon flew into a rage and struck Jizhen from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: During the review of Gansu campaign honors, Jizhen petitioned to restore former Grand Coordinator Mei Zhihuan to office; the emperor erupted in anger and removed Jizhen from the register.

sentences.zh: 已，論四川桃紅壩功，復官，致仕。

translations.literal: Later, when Sichuan achievements at Taohongba were reviewed, his office was restored and he retired.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when honors were granted for the Taohongba campaign in Sichuan, his rank was restored and he retired.

sentences.zh: 十一年用薦起，歷兩京尚寶卿。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was raised on recommendation and served in succession as court of imperial seals minister in both capitals.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was recalled on recommendation and served successively as court of imperial seals minister in both capitals.

sentences.zh: 明年春召對，陳水利屯田甚悉，遷順天府丞。

translations.literal: The next spring he was summoned for an audience and set forth water conservancy and military colonies in great detail; he was transferred to vice director of the Shuntian prefectural administration commission.
translations.idiomatic: The following spring he was summoned to audience and laid out a detailed plan for irrigation and military colonies; he was promoted to vice director of the Shuntian prefectural administration commission.

sentences.zh: 尋超拜兵部右侍郎兼右僉都御史，巡撫天津，督薊、遼軍餉。

translations.literal: Soon he was abruptly promoted to vice minister of the Ministry of War and right vice censor-in-chief, grand coordinator of Tianjin, supervising military rations for Ji and Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon elevated to vice minister of the Ministry of War and right vice censor-in-chief, sent out as grand coordinator of Tianjin to oversee military rations for Ji and Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 乃大興屯田，列上經地、招佃、用水、任人、薄賦五議。

translations.literal: Thereupon he greatly expanded military colonies and submitted five proposals on surveying land, recruiting tenants, managing water, appointing men, and lightening levies.
translations.idiomatic: He then launched a major program of military colonies and submitted five proposals on land surveys, tenant recruitment, water management, personnel, and tax relief.

sentences.zh: 白塘、葛沽數十里間，田大熟。

translations.literal: Within the several tens of li between Baitang and Gegu, the fields had a great harvest.
translations.idiomatic: For dozens of li around Baitang and Gegu, the farmland yielded an abundant harvest.

sentences.zh: 十四年冬，詔發水師援遼，坐戰艦不具，除名。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fourteenth year, an edict ordered the naval force sent to aid Liaodong; on account of warships not being ready, he was struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, the court ordered the navy to reinforce Liaodong; because his warships were not ready, he was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 明年夏，召為兵部添註右侍郎。

translations.literal: The next summer he was summoned to serve as an additionally appointed right vice minister of the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: The following summer he was recalled as concurrently appointed right vice minister of the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 得疾，卒於途。

translations.literal: He fell ill and died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: He took ill and died en route.

sentences.zh: 是夕，星隕中庭。

translations.literal: That evening, a star fell in the central courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: That same night, a meteor fell in the courtyard.

sentences.zh: 贈右都御史，官一子。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the title of right censor-in-chief, and one son was given an official appointment.
translations.idiomatic: The court posthumously honored him as right censor-in-chief and granted an official post to one of his sons.

sentences.zh: 方震孺，字孩未，桐城人，移家壽州。

translations.literal: Fang Zhenru, style Haiwei, was a native of Tongcheng and moved his household to Shouzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Zhenru, whose style name was Haiwei, came from Tongcheng but later moved his family to Shouzhou.

sentences.zh: 萬歷四十一年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the forty-first year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his jinshi degree in the forty-first year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 由沙縣知縣入為御史。

translations.literal: From magistrate of Shaxian County he entered service as a censor.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from magistrate of Shaxian County to become a censor at court.

sentences.zh: 遼陽既破，震孺一日十三疏，請增巡撫，通海運，調邊兵，易司馬。

translations.literal: After Liaoyang fell, Zhenru submitted thirteen memorials in one day, requesting additional grand coordinators, opening sea transport, redeploying frontier troops, and replacing the regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: Once Liaoyang had fallen, Zhenru filed thirteen memorials in a single day, calling for more grand coordinators, resumed maritime supply lines, redeployment of frontier troops, and replacement of the regional commander.

sentences.zh: 日五鼓撾公卿門，籌畫痛哭，而自請犒師。

translations.literal: Each day at the fifth watch he beat on the gates of high officials, planning and weeping bitterly, and himself requested to reward the troops.
translations.idiomatic: Every day before dawn he hammered on the doors of ranking officials, weeping as he laid out his plans, and volunteered to go distribute rewards to the army himself.

sentences.zh: 是時，三岔河以西四百里，人煙絕，軍民盡竄，文武將吏無一騎東者。

translations.literal: At that time, for four hundred li west of Sancha River, human habitation was extinct; soldiers and civilians had all fled, and among civil and military officers and generals not a single rider went east.
translations.idiomatic: At that point, for four hundred li west of the Sancha River the land was utterly deserted; troops and civilians had all fled, and not one civil or military official rode eastward.

sentences.zh: 帝壯其言，發帑金二十萬震孺犒師。

translations.literal: The emperor was stirred by his words and issued two hundred thousand taels from the treasury for Zhenru to reward the troops.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by his plea, the emperor released two hundred thousand taels from the imperial treasury for Zhenru to use in rewarding the troops.

sentences.zh: 六月，震孺出關，延見將士，吊死扶傷，軍民大悅。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Zhenru went beyond the pass, summoned and received officers and soldiers, mourned the dead and tended the wounded, and the army and people were greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Zhenru crossed the frontier, met with officers and men, consoled the dead and cared for the wounded, winning the deep gratitude of soldiers and civilians alike.

sentences.zh: 因上言：「河廣不七十步，一葦可航，非有驚濤怒浪之險，不足恃者一。

translations.literal: Thereupon he submitted a memorial: "The river is no more than seventy paces wide; a single reed can ferry across; there are no dangers of crashing waves or raging billows — the first thing not to be relied upon.
translations.idiomatic: He then memorialized: "The river is less than seventy paces across—a reed raft can cross it—and there are no treacherous surges or raging waters. That is the first reason not to trust it as a barrier.

sentences.zh: 兵來，斬木為排，浮以土，多人推之，如履平地，不足恃者二。

translations.literal: When troops come, they can hew timber into rafts, float them with earth, and many men push them as if walking on level ground — the second thing not to be relied upon.
translations.idiomatic: When enemy troops arrive, they can chop timber into rafts, load them with earth, and push them across with many hands as easily as walking dry land. That is the second reason.

sentences.zh: 河去代子河不遠，兵從代子徑渡，守河之卒不滿二萬，能望其半渡而遏之乎？

translations.literal: The river is not far from the Daizi River; troops can cross directly from Daizi; the soldiers guarding the river are fewer than twenty thousand — can one hope to stop them when half have crossed?
translations.idiomatic: The river lies close to the Daizi River, allowing troops to ford there directly. With fewer than twenty thousand men guarding the river, how could we hope to intercept them halfway across?

sentences.zh: 不足恃者三。

translations.literal: The third thing not to be relied upon.
translations.idiomatic: That is the third reason it cannot be trusted.

sentences.zh: 沿河百六十里，築城則不能，列柵則無用，不足恃者四。

translations.literal: Along the river for one hundred sixty li, building walls is impossible and setting palisades is useless — the fourth thing not to be relied upon.
translations.idiomatic: For one hundred sixty li along the river, we cannot build walls and palisades would be useless. That is the fourth reason.

sentences.zh: 黃泥窪、張叉站沖淺之處，可修守，今地非我有，不足恃者五。

translations.literal: At Huangniwa and Zhangchazhan, the shallow fords can be fortified and defended, but now the land is not ours — the fifth thing not to be relied upon.
translations.idiomatic: The shallow crossings at Huangniwa and Zhangchazhan could be held, but that ground is no longer in our hands. That is the fifth reason.

sentences.zh: 轉眼冰合，遂成平地，間次置防，猶得五十萬人，兵從何來？

translations.literal: In the blink of an eye the ice will join and it becomes level ground; placing defenses at intervals would still require five hundred thousand men — from where would the troops come?
translations.idiomatic: Before long the ice will freeze solid and the river will become open plain. Even spaced defenses would need five hundred thousand men—where would such an army come from?

sentences.zh: 不足恃者六。」

translations.literal: The sixth thing not to be relied upon."
translations.idiomatic: That is the sixth reason."

sentences.zh: 又言：「我以退為守，則守不足；

translations.literal: He also said: "If we take retreat as defense, then defense is insufficient;
translations.idiomatic: He also argued: "If we make retreat our strategy of defense, our defenses will never suffice;

sentences.zh: 我以進為守，則守有余。

translations.literal: if we take advance as defense, then defense is more than sufficient.
translations.idiomatic: but if we make advance our strategy of defense, our defenses will be more than adequate.

sentences.zh: 專倚三岔作家，萬一時事偶非，榆關一線遂足鎖薊門哉？」

translations.literal: Relying solely on making a home at Sancha — if by chance the times go against us, is the single thread of Yugu Pass alone enough to lock the gate of Ji?"
translations.idiomatic: To stake everything on Sancha alone—if fortune turns against us, can Yugu Pass's thin line truly seal off the gateway to Ji?"

sentences.zh: 疏入，帝命震孺巡按遼東，監紀軍事。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, the emperor ordered Zhenru to inspect Liaodong and supervise military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After the memorial was received, the emperor appointed Zhenru touring censor of Liaodong with authority to oversee military affairs.

sentences.zh: 震孺按遼，居不廬、食不火者七月。

translations.literal: Zhenru inspected Liaodong; for seven months he dwelt without a hut and ate without cooked food.
translations.idiomatic: During his inspection of Liaodong, Zhenru went seven months without proper shelter or cooked meals.

sentences.zh: 議者欲棄三岔河，退守廣寧，震孺請駐兵振武。

translations.literal: Those in council wished to abandon the Sancha River and fall back to defend Guangning; Zhenru requested troops be stationed at Zhenwu.
translations.idiomatic: Some officials wanted to abandon the Sancha River and withdraw to Guangning, but Zhenru urged that troops be posted at Zhenwu.

sentences.zh: 軍法不嚴，震孺請敕寧前監軍，專斬逃軍逃將。

translations.literal: Military law was not strict; Zhenru requested an edict to the military supervisor before Ning, exclusively to execute deserters and fleeing generals.
translations.idiomatic: Because military discipline was lax, Zhenru asked that the frontier supervisor before Ning be empowered to execute deserters and fleeing officers without further appeal.

sentences.zh: 並從其言。

translations.literal: All were granted according to his words.
translations.idiomatic: The court accepted all of his recommendations.

sentences.zh: 然是時，經撫不和，疆事益壞。

translations.literal: Yet at that time the regional commander and grand coordinator were not in harmony, and frontier affairs grew ever worse.
translations.idiomatic: But by then the regional commander and grand coordinator were at odds, and the frontier situation deteriorated further.

sentences.zh: 震孺再疏言山海無外衛，宜亟駐兵中前，以為眼目，不省。

translations.literal: Zhenru again memorialized that Shanhai had no outer defense and troops should urgently be stationed at Zhongqian as eyes and ears; it was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenru memorialized again that Shanhaiguan lacked outer defenses and that troops should immediately be posted at Zhongqian as forward watchpoints; the court ignored him.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，任滿，候代前屯，而大清兵已再渡三岔河。

translations.literal: In the first month of the next year, his term expired; he awaited his replacement at Qiantun, while the Great Qing army had already crossed the Sancha River a second time.
translations.idiomatic: The following first month, as his term ended and he waited for his successor at Qiantun, Qing forces had already crossed the Sancha River for the second time.

sentences.zh: 先鋒孫得功不戰，而呼於振武曰「兵敗矣」，遂走。

translations.literal: The vanguard Sun Degong did not fight but shouted at Zhenwu, "The army is defeated!" and then fled.
translations.idiomatic: The vanguard Sun Degong refused to fight, shouted "We're beaten!" at Zhenwu, and fled.

sentences.zh: 巡撫王化貞在廣寧，亦倉皇走。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Wang Huazhen was at Guangning and also fled in panic.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Wang Huazhen, stationed at Guangning, fled in disarray as well.

sentences.zh: 列城聞之皆走，惟震孺前屯無動。

translations.literal: The walled cities, hearing this, all fled; only Zhenru at Qiantun did not stir.
translations.idiomatic: Every fortified town took flight upon hearing the news—only Zhenru at Qiantun held his ground.

sentences.zh: 當是時，西平守將羅一貫已戰死，參將祖大壽擁殘兵駐覺華島上。

translations.literal: At that time the garrison commander of Xiping, Luo Yiguan, had already died in battle, and vice commander Zu Dashou held remnant troops stationed on Juehua Island.
translations.idiomatic: By then Xiping's garrison commander Luo Yiguan had fallen in battle, and Vice Commander Zu Dashou had gathered the survivors on Juehua Island.

sentences.zh: 於是震孺召水師帥張國卿相與謀曰：「今東師四外搜糧，聞祖將軍在島上有米豆二十余萬，兵十余萬，人民數萬，戰艦、器仗、馬牛無數，東師即媾得島兵，得島兵以攻榆關，豈有幸哉？」

translations.literal: Thereupon Zhenru summoned the naval commander Zhang Guoqing to consult together, saying: "Now the eastern army is searching for grain in all directions; I hear General Zu on the island has more than two hundred thousand shi of grain and beans, more than one hundred thousand troops, tens of thousands of people, and countless warships, weapons, horses, and oxen. If the eastern army even makes peace and obtains the island's troops, and with island troops attacks Yugu Pass — would there be any luck?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhenru then summoned naval commander Zhang Guoqing to plan together: "The Qing army is scouring the countryside for supplies. General Zu reportedly has over two hundred thousand shi of grain on the island, more than one hundred thousand soldiers, tens of thousands of civilians, and abundant warships, arms, horses, and cattle. If the Qing forces pacify him and seize his army to strike Yugu Pass, what hope would we have?"

sentences.zh: 於是震孺、國卿航海見大壽，慷慨語曰：「將軍歸，相保以富貴；

translations.literal: Thereupon Zhenru and Guoqing sailed to see Dashou and spoke passionately: "General, if you return, we shall secure each other in wealth and honor;
translations.idiomatic: So Zhenru and Guoqing sailed to meet Dashou and spoke with passion: "General, if you come back with us, we will see you honored and enriched;

sentences.zh: 不歸，震孺請以頸血濺將軍。」

translations.literal: if you do not return, Zhenru asks to splash the general with the blood of his neck."
translations.idiomatic: if you refuse, I ask leave to die here and stain you with my blood."

sentences.zh: 大壽泣，震孺亦泣，遂相攜以歸，獲軍民輜重無算。

translations.literal: Dashou wept, Zhenru also wept, and they then went back hand in hand, obtaining incalculable military and civilian baggage.
translations.idiomatic: Dashou wept, Zhenru wept as well, and they returned together, bringing back an incalculable store of troops, civilians, and supplies.

sentences.zh: 有主事徐大化者，忠賢黨也，劾震孺曰「攘差」。

translations.literal: There was a director Xu Dahua, a partisan of Zhongxian, who impeached Zhenru saying "seizing another's commission."
translations.idiomatic: One director Xu Dahua, a follower of Wei Zhongxian, impeached Zhenru for overstepping his assigned duties.

sentences.zh: 都御史鄒元標奮筆曰：「方御史保全山海，無過且有社稷功。」

translations.literal: Censor-in-chief Zou Yuanbiao wrote vigorously: "Investigator Fang preserved Shanhai; he had no fault and indeed had merit for the altars of soil and grain."
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-chief Zou Yuanbiao wrote forcefully in his defense: "Investigator Fang saved Shanhaiguan and its hinterland—not only without fault but with service to the realm."

sentences.zh: 給事中郭興治遂借道學以逐元標。

translations.literal: The supervising secretary Guo Xingzhi then used Daoxue as a pretext to drive Yuanbiao out.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary Guo Xingzhi then used accusations of partisan learning to force Yuanbiao from office.

sentences.zh: 元標去，震孺亦即罷歸。

translations.literal: Yuanbiao departed, and Zhenru likewise was dismissed and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: With Yuanbiao gone, Zhenru was also dismissed and sent home.

sentences.zh: 明年，忠賢、廣微興大獄，再募劾方御史者，興治再論震孺河西贓私。

translations.literal: The next year, Zhongxian and Guangwei launched a great inquisition, again recruiting accusers of Investigator Fang; Xingzhi again indicted Zhenru for corruption west of the river.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Zhongxian and Wei Guangwei opened a major purge, recruiting new accusers against Investigator Fang; Guo Xingzhi renewed charges of embezzlement against Zhenru west of the river.

sentences.zh: 逮問掠治，坐贓六千有奇，擬絞。

translations.literal: He was arrested and interrogated under torture; found guilty of more than six thousand in illicit gains, death by strangulation was proposed.
translations.idiomatic: Arrested and tortured under interrogation, he was convicted of embezzling more than six thousand taels and sentenced to strangulation.

sentences.zh: 而揚州守劉鐸咒詛之獄又起，遂誣震孺與交通，坐大辟，系獄。

translations.literal: Then the case of Yangzhou prefect Liu Duo for cursing arose, and they falsely accused Zhenru of association with him; he was convicted of the great penalty and imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: When the case of Yangzhou prefect Liu Duo for casting curses erupted, Zhenru was falsely implicated as his accomplice, condemned to death, and thrown into prison.
