sentences.zh: 有邏卒時時佐震孺飲啖，問之，則曰：「小人有妻，聞公精忠，手治以獻者也。」

translations.literal: There was a prison guard who from time to time provided Zhenru food and drink; asked about it, he said: "This petty man has a wife; hearing of your utmost loyalty, she prepared it by hand to offer."
translations.idiomatic: A prison guard sometimes brought Zhenru food and drink; when asked, he said, "My wife, hearing of your steadfast loyalty, prepared this herself as an offering to you."

sentences.zh: 輒報珰曰：「某病革，某瀕死。」

translations.literal: He would then report to the eunuch: "So-and-so is gravely ill, so-and-so is near death."
translations.idiomatic: He would then tell the eunuch agents, "So-and-so is deathly ill" or "So-and-so is at death's door."

sentences.zh: 珰以是防益疏。

translations.literal: The eunuchs therefore grew ever laxer in their guard.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch handlers, believing this, slackened their watch ever further.

sentences.zh: 明年，莊烈帝嗣位，得釋還。

translations.literal: The next year, when the Chongzhen Emperor succeeded to the throne, he was released and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, upon the Chongzhen Emperor's accession, he was freed and allowed to go home.

sentences.zh: 八年春，流賊犯壽州，州長吏適遷秩去，震孺倡士民固守，賊自是不敢逼壽州。

translations.literal: In the spring of the eighth year, bandit rebels attacked Shouzhou; the prefectural chief official happened to be transferred away; Zhenru rallied gentry and people to hold firm, and the rebels themselves did not dare press Shouzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the eighth year, rebel bands besieged Shouzhou just as its chief magistrate was transferred elsewhere; Zhenru rallied local gentry and townspeople to hold the city, and the rebels never dared approach.

sentences.zh: 巡撫史可法上其功，用為廣西參議。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Shi Kefa reported his merit, and he was appointed Guangxi administrative vice commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Shi Kefa memorialized his achievement, and he was appointed administrative vice commissioner of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 尋擢右僉都御史，巡撫廣西。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to right vice censor-in-chief, grand coordinator of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to right vice censor-in-chief and appointed grand coordinator of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 京師陷，福王立南京，即日拜疏勤王。

translations.literal: When the capital fell, the Prince of Fu established himself at Nanjing; that very day he submitted a memorial to rescue the throne.
translations.idiomatic: After Beijing fell and the Prince of Fu was enthroned at Nanjing, Zhenru immediately submitted a memorial offering to march to the emperor's aid.

sentences.zh: 馬士英、阮大鋮憚之，敕還鎮。

translations.literal: Ma Shiying and Ruan Dacheng feared him and ordered him back to his post.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Shiying and Ruan Dacheng, wary of him, ordered him to return to his jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 震孺竟郁郁憂憤而卒。

translations.literal: Zhenru ultimately died of gloom, worry, and indignation.
translations.idiomatic: In the end Zhenru died of grief and suppressed rage.

sentences.zh: 徐從治，字仲華，海鹽人。

translations.literal: Xu Congzhi, style Zhonghua, was a native of Haiyan.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Congzhi, whose style name was Zhonghua, came from Haiyan.

sentences.zh: 母夢神人舞戈於庭，寤而生。

translations.literal: His mother dreamed of a divine man dancing with a halberd in the courtyard; waking, she gave birth.
translations.idiomatic: His mother dreamed of a god dancing with a halberd in the courtyard, and gave birth to him upon waking.

sentences.zh: 從治舉萬歷三十五年進士，除桐城知縣。

translations.literal: Congzhi passed the jinshi examination in the thirty-fifth year of Wanli and was appointed magistrate of Tongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Congzhi earned his jinshi in the thirty-fifth year of Wanli and was appointed magistrate of Tongcheng.

sentences.zh: 累官濟南知府，以卓異遷兗東副使，駐沂州。

translations.literal: Through successive posts he became prefect of Jinan; for outstanding performance he was transferred to eastern Yan deputy commissioner, stationed at Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to prefect of Jinan, then—marked for exceptional service—was promoted to eastern Yan deputy commissioner, based at Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 天啟元年，妖賊徐鴻儒反鄆城，連陷鄒、滕、嶧縣。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianqi, the sorcerer-rebel Xu Hongru revolted at Yuncheng and in succession captured Zou, Teng, and Yi counties.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianqi, the sorcerer-rebel Xu Hongru rose at Yuncheng and swiftly overran Zou, Teng, and Yi counties.

sentences.zh: 從治捕得其黨之伏沂者殺之，請就家起故總兵楊肇基主兵事，而獻搗賊中堅之策，遂滅鴻儒。

translations.literal: Congzhi captured and killed his partisans hiding at Yi, requested the former regional commander Yang Zhaoji be recalled from retirement to lead military affairs, and submitted a plan to strike the rebel core; thereby Hongru was destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Congzhi rooted out and executed Hongru's agents hidden in Yizhou, petitioned to recall retired regional commander Yang Zhaoji to command the campaign, and proposed a strategy to destroy the rebel core—bringing about Hongru's defeat.

sentences.zh: 事詳《趙彥傳》。

translations.literal: The affair is detailed in the biography of Zhao Yan.
translations.idiomatic: The full account appears in the biography of Zhao Yan.

sentences.zh: 從治警敏通變，其禦賊類主剿不主撫，故往往滅賊。

translations.literal: Congzhi was alert, sharp, and adaptable; in dealing with bandits he generally favored extermination over pacification, and so often destroyed bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Quick-witted and resourceful, Congzhi generally favored crushing rebels over negotiating with them, and repeatedly succeeded in wiping them out.

sentences.zh: 旋以右參政分守濟南。

translations.literal: Soon he was made right administrative vice commissioner with divided defense of Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed right administrative vice commissioner with responsibility for the Jinan circuit.

sentences.zh: 錄功，從治最，進右布政使，督漕江南。

translations.literal: Recording merit, Congzhi ranked highest; he was promoted to right administration commissioner and supervised grain transport in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: When rewards were tallied, Congzhi's service ranked first; he was promoted to right administration commissioner and put in charge of grain transport on the Jiangnan route.

sentences.zh: 妖賊再起，巡撫王惟儉奏留從治，仍守沂。

translations.literal: Sorcerer-rebels rose again; Grand Coordinator Wang Weijian memorialized to retain Congzhi, still guarding Yi.
translations.idiomatic: When sorcerer-rebels rose again, Grand Coordinator Wang Weijian petitioned to keep Congzhi in Shandong, still stationed at Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 按臣主撫，從治議不合，遂告歸。

translations.literal: The touring censor favored pacification; Congzhi's views did not agree, and he therefore requested to return home.
translations.idiomatic: The touring censor favored a conciliatory approach, which Congzhi opposed; he resigned and returned home.

sentences.zh: 中外計議調，崇禎初，以故秩飭薊州兵備。

translations.literal: Within and without, plans were debated for his transfer; at the beginning of Chongzhen, at his former rank he was put in charge of Jizhou military preparedness.
translations.idiomatic: After deliberation at court and in the provinces, he was recalled at the start of the Chongzhen reign, at his former rank, to oversee military preparedness at Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 薊軍久缺餉，圍巡撫王應豸於遵化。

translations.literal: The Ji army had long lacked rations and surrounded Grand Coordinator Wang Yingzhi at Zunhua.
translations.idiomatic: Long deprived of pay, the Ji garrison mutinied and besieged Grand Coordinator Wang Yingzhi at Zunhua.

sentences.zh: 從治單騎馳入，陰部署夷丁、標兵，分營四門，按甲不動，登城而呼曰：「給三月糧，趣歸守汛地，否將擊汝！」

translations.literal: Congzhi rode alone and galloped in; secretly deploying foreign troops and standard soldiers, he divided camps at the four gates, kept armor on and did not move, climbed the wall and shouted: "Give three months' rations; hurry back to guard your posts, or I will strike you!"
translations.idiomatic: Congzhi rode in alone, secretly positioning foreign auxiliaries and regular troops at all four gates. Without drawing weapons, he mounted the wall and shouted: "Issue three months' pay and send them back to their posts—or I will attack you!"

sentences.zh: 眾應聲而散。

translations.literal: The crowd at the sound dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: The mutineers dispersed at once.

sentences.zh: 其應變多類此。

translations.literal: His adaptation to changing circumstances was mostly of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: He handled crises in this manner again and again.

sentences.zh: 進秩左布政使，再請告歸。

translations.literal: His rank was advanced to left administration commissioner; he again requested leave to return home.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to left administration commissioner, he once more petitioned to retire.

sentences.zh: 四年，起飭武德兵備。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he was raised to oversee military preparedness at Wude.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was recalled to oversee military preparedness in the Wude circuit.

sentences.zh: 孔有德反山東，巡撫余大成檄從治監軍。

translations.literal: Kong Youde rebelled in Shandong; Grand Coordinator Yu Dacheng ordered Congzhi to supervise the army.
translations.idiomatic: When Kong Youde rebelled in Shandong, Grand Coordinator Yu Dacheng dispatched Congzhi to supervise the campaign.

sentences.zh: 明年正月馳赴萊州，而登州已陷。

translations.literal: In the first month of the next year he raced to Laizhou, but Dengzhou had already fallen.
translations.idiomatic: The following first month he rushed to Laizhou, only to find Dengzhou already lost.

sentences.zh: 大成削籍，遂擢從治右副都御史代之，與登萊巡撫謝璉並命。

translations.literal: Dacheng was struck from the rolls; Congzhi was then promoted to right vice censor-in-chief to replace him, appointed together with Deng-Lai Grand Coordinator Xie Lian.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Dacheng was dismissed from the rolls; Congzhi was promoted to right vice censor-in-chief to replace him, receiving simultaneous appointment alongside Deng-Lai Grand Coordinator Xie Lian.

sentences.zh: 詔璉駐萊州，從治駐青州，調度兵食。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Lian to be stationed at Laizhou and Congzhi at Qingzhou, coordinating troops and provisions.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Xie Lian to base himself at Laizhou and Congzhi at Qingzhou to coordinate troops and supplies.

sentences.zh: 從治曰：「吾駐青，不足鎮萊人心；

translations.literal: Congzhi said: "If I am stationed at Qing, it is insufficient to stabilize the hearts of Laizhou;
translations.idiomatic: Congzhi argued: "Stationing me at Qingzhou won't steady morale in Laizhou;

sentences.zh: 駐萊，足系全齊命。」

translations.literal: if stationed at Lai, it is sufficient to tie the fate of all Qi."
translations.idiomatic: but basing myself at Laizhou would hold all of Shandong together."

sentences.zh: 乃與璉同受事於萊。

translations.literal: He then together with Lian received their commissions at Lai.
translations.idiomatic: He and Xie Lian therefore both took up their posts at Laizhou.

sentences.zh: 有德者，遼人。

translations.literal: Youde was a man of Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Youde was a native of Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 與耿仲明、李九成、毛承祿輩皆毛文龍帳下卒也。

translations.literal: He, together with Geng Zhongming, Li Jiucheng, Mao Chenglu, and others, were all soldiers under Mao Wenlong's command.
translations.idiomatic: He, along with Geng Zhongming, Li Jiucheng, Mao Chenglu, and others, had all served as soldiers under Mao Wenlong.

sentences.zh: 文龍死，走入登州。

translations.literal: When Wenlong died, they fled into Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Wenlong's death, they fled to Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 登萊巡撫孫元化官遼久，素言遼人可用，乃用承祿為副將，有德、仲明為遊擊，九成為偏裨，且多收遼人為牙兵。

translations.literal: Deng-Lai Grand Coordinator Sun Yuanhua had long served in Liaodong and always said Liaodong men could be used; he therefore appointed Chenglu as vice general, Youde and Zhongming as mobile brigade commanders, Jiucheng as a staff officer, and moreover took in many Liaodong men as personal guard soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Deng-Lai Grand Coordinator Sun Yuanhua, a longtime Liaodong official who insisted Liaodong veterans were trustworthy, appointed Mao Chenglu vice general, Kong Youde and Geng Zhongming as mobile brigade commanders, Li Jiucheng as a staff officer, and recruited many Liaodong men as his personal guard.

sentences.zh: 是年，大淩河新城被圍，部檄元化發勁卒泛海，趨耀州鹽場，示牽制。

translations.literal: That year, when Dalinghe New City was besieged, the ministry ordered Yuanhua to dispatch crack troops by sea toward the Yaozhou salt fields to show diversion.
translations.idiomatic: That year, as Dalinghe New City came under siege, the ministry ordered Yuanhua to send elite troops by sea toward the Yaozhou salt fields as a diversion.

sentences.zh: 有德詭言風逆，改從陸赴寧遠。

translations.literal: Youde falsely claimed the wind was contrary and changed to go by land toward Ningyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Youde falsely claimed adverse winds and diverted the march overland toward Ningyuan instead.

sentences.zh: 十月晦，有德及九成子千總應元統千余人以行，經月抵吳橋，縣人罷市，眾無所得食。

translations.literal: On the last day of the tenth month, Youde and Jiucheng's son, company commander Yingyuan, leading more than a thousand men on the march, after a month reached Wuqiao; the county people closed the markets and the crowd obtained no food.
translations.idiomatic: On the last day of the tenth month, Youde set out with more than a thousand men under Li Jiucheng's son, company commander Yingyuan. After a month on the road they reached Wuqiao, where townspeople had shut the markets and the troops found nothing to eat.

sentences.zh: 一卒與諸生角，有德抶之，眾大嘩。

translations.literal: One soldier quarreled with a student; Youde flogged him, and the crowd raised a great uproar.
translations.idiomatic: When a soldier quarreled with a local scholar, Youde had him beaten, provoking a general uproar.

sentences.zh: 九成先賫元化銀市馬塞上，用盡無以償，適至吳橋。

translations.literal: Jiucheng had first been entrusted with Yuanhua's silver to buy horses on the frontier; it was exhausted with nothing to repay; he happened to arrive at Wuqiao.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jiucheng had earlier been given Sun Yuanhua's silver to buy horses on the frontier, spent it all without accounting for it, and happened to arrive at Wuqiao just then.

sentences.zh: 聞眾怨，遂與應元謀，劫有德，相與為亂，陷陵縣、臨邑、商河，殘齊東，圍德平。

translations.literal: Hearing the crowd's resentment, he then with Yingyuan plotted, coerced Youde, and together made rebellion; they captured Ling, Linyi, and Shanghe counties, ravaged eastern Qi, and besieged Deping.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the men's anger, he conspired with Yingyuan to coerce Youde into mutiny; together they plundered Ling, Linyi, and Shanghe, ravaged eastern Shandong, and besieged Deping.

sentences.zh: 既而舍去，陷青城、新城，整眾東。

translations.literal: Soon they abandoned these and captured Qingcheng and Xincheng, reorganized their forces and marched east.
translations.idiomatic: They then abandoned those targets, seized Qingcheng and Xincheng, regrouped, and marched eastward.

sentences.zh: 余大成者，江寧人也。

translations.literal: Yu Dacheng was a man of Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Dacheng was a native of Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 不知兵。

translations.literal: He did not understand military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He knew nothing of military matters.

sentences.zh: 初為職方，嘗奏發大學士劉一燝私書，齮之去。

translations.literal: At first he was in the Bureau of Appointments; he once memorialized exposing Grand Secretary Liu Yihuan's private letters and drove him out through calumny.
translations.idiomatic: Early in his career he served in the Bureau of Appointments; he once exposed Grand Secretary Liu Yihuan's private correspondence and forced his removal through factional attack.

sentences.zh: 後又以事忤魏忠賢，削籍歸，有清執名。

translations.literal: Later he again on account of matters offended Wei Zhongxian, was struck from the rolls and returned home, having a reputation for upright integrity.
translations.idiomatic: He later clashed with Wei Zhongxian, was dismissed from the rolls, and returned home with a reputation for upright integrity.

sentences.zh: 而巡撫山東，則白蓮妖賊方熾，又有逃兵之變，皆不能討。

translations.literal: Yet as grand coordinator of Shandong, the White Lotus sorcerer-rebels were then blazing, and there were also mutinies of deserters — all of which he could not suppress.
translations.idiomatic: Yet as grand coordinator of Shandong, he proved unable to put down the raging White Lotus rebels or the mutiny of deserting soldiers.

sentences.zh: 及聞有德叛，即托疾數日不能出，不得已遣中軍沈廷諭參將陶廷鑨往禦，則皆敗而走。

translations.literal: When he heard Youde had rebelled, he immediately feigned illness and for several days could not go out; compelled, he sent headquarters officer Shen Tingyu and brigade commander Tao Tingxun to resist — they were both defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: On hearing of Kong Youde's rebellion, he promptly feigned illness and stayed indoors for days; only under pressure did he dispatch Shen Tingyu and Tao Tingxun to oppose the rebels — both were routed and fled.

sentences.zh: 大成恐，遂定議撫，而元化軍亦至。

translations.literal: Dacheng grew afraid, and so settled on a policy of pacification; Yuanhua's army also arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Yu Dacheng resolved on a policy of appeasement, just as Sun Yuanhua's troops arrived.

sentences.zh: 元化者，故所號善西洋大炮者也，至是亦主撫，檄賊所過郡縣無邀擊。

translations.literal: Yuanhua was the one formerly styled as skilled with Western cannon; at this time he also advocated pacification, and issued orders to the prefectures and counties the rebels passed through not to intercept them.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yuanhua — once famed for his mastery of Western artillery — now likewise favored appeasement, ordering every prefecture and county in the rebels' path to hold their fire.

sentences.zh: 賊長驅，無敢一矢加者。

translations.literal: The rebels drove straight through; none dared shoot a single arrow at them.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels marched unopposed, and not a single arrow was fired in their direction.

sentences.zh: 賊佯許元化降。

translations.literal: The rebels feigned agreeing to Yuanhua's surrender terms.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels pretended to accept Sun Yuanhua's offer of surrender.

sentences.zh: 元化師次黃山館而返，賊遂抵登州。

translations.literal: Yuanhua's army halted at Huangshan Station and returned; the rebels then reached Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yuanhua halted his army at Huangshan Station and withdrew, and the rebels pressed on to Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 元化遣將張燾率遼兵駐城外，總兵張可大率南兵拒賊。

translations.literal: Yuanhua sent the general Zhang Tao leading Liaodong troops to encamp outside the walls; regional commander Zhang Keda led southern troops to resist the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yuanhua posted Zhang Tao with Liaodong troops outside the city while regional commander Zhang Keda led southern troops to hold the rebels at bay.

sentences.zh: 元化猶招降賊，賊不應。

translations.literal: Yuanhua still summoned the rebels to surrender; the rebels did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yuanhua continued to negotiate surrender, but the rebels ignored him.

sentences.zh: 五年正月戰城東，遼兵遽退，南兵遂敗。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifth year they fought east of the city; the Liaodong troops suddenly retreated, and the southern troops were then defeated.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year five they fought east of the city; the Liaodong troops broke ranks at once, and the southern force was routed.

sentences.zh: 燾兵多降賊，賊遣之歸，士民爭請拒勿內，元化不從，賊遂入。

translations.literal: Many of Tao's soldiers surrendered to the rebels; the rebels sent them back, and the gentry and commoners all petitioned to refuse them entry — Yuanhua did not comply, and the rebels thus entered.
translations.idiomatic: Many of Zhang Tao's men defected and were sent back by the rebels; townspeople begged to keep them out, but Sun Yuanhua refused — and the rebels walked in.

sentences.zh: 日夕，城中火起，中軍耿仲明、都司陳光福等導賊入自東門，城遂陷。

translations.literal: At dusk, fires broke out in the city; headquarters officer Geng Zhongming, company commander Chen Guangfu, and others guided the rebels in through the east gate, and the city then fell.
translations.idiomatic: By evening fires were burning inside the walls; Geng Zhongming, Chen Guangfu, and others opened the east gate to the rebels, and the city fell.

sentences.zh: 可大死之。

translations.literal: Keda died in the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Keda was killed.

sentences.zh: 元化自刎不殊，與參議宋光蘭、僉事王征及府縣官悉被執。

translations.literal: Yuanhua cut his own throat but did not die; together with administrative commissioner Song Guanglan, supervising secretary Wang Zheng, and all prefectural and county officials, he was entirely seized.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yuanhua slashed his own throat but survived; Song Guanglan, Wang Zheng, and every prefectural and county official were taken prisoner.

sentences.zh: 大成馳入萊州。

translations.literal: Dacheng galloped into Laizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Dacheng fled posthaste to Laizhou.

sentences.zh: 初，登州被圍，朝廷鐫大成、元化三級，令辦賊。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Dengzhou was besieged, the court reduced Dacheng and Yuanhua three grades in rank and ordered them to suppress the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: When Dengzhou first came under siege, the court cut Yu Dacheng and Sun Yuanhua three ranks and ordered them to destroy the rebels.

sentences.zh: 及登失守，革元化職，而以謝璉代。

translations.literal: When Deng fell, Yuanhua's office was abolished and Xie Lian was appointed in his place.
translations.idiomatic: After Dengzhou fell, Sun Yuanhua was dismissed and replaced by Xie Lian.

sentences.zh: 有德既破登州，推九成為主，己次之，仲明又次之。

translations.literal: Youde, having taken Dengzhou, set up Jiucheng as leader, with himself second and Zhongming third.
translations.idiomatic: After capturing Dengzhou, Kong Youde installed Li Jiucheng as chief, with himself second and Geng Zhongming third in rank.

sentences.zh: 用巡撫印檄州縣餉，趣元化移書求撫於大成曰：「畀以登州一郡，則解。」

translations.literal: Using the grand coordinator's seal, they issued requisition orders to prefectures and counties for supplies, and pressed Yuanhua to send a letter seeking pacification through Dacheng, saying: "Grant us the single prefecture of Dengzhou, and we will stand down."
translations.idiomatic: Using the grand coordinator's seal they requisitioned supplies from surrounding counties and had Sun Yuanhua write Yu Dacheng proposing appeasement: "Give us Dengzhou prefecture and we will dissolve."

sentences.zh: 大成聞於朝。

translations.literal: Dacheng reported this to the court.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Dacheng relayed the proposal to the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，命革大成職，而以從治代。

translations.literal: The emperor grew angry and ordered Dacheng dismissed from office, appointing Congzhi in his place.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was incensed, dismissed Yu Dacheng, and installed Xu Congzhi in his stead.

sentences.zh: 先是，賊攻破黃縣，知縣吳世揚死之。

translations.literal: Earlier, the rebels had stormed Huang County; Magistrate Wu Shiyang died in the defense.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels had already overrun Huang County, where Magistrate Wu Shiyang died fighting.

sentences.zh: 至是，攻萊，從治、璉與總兵楊禦蕃等分陴守。

translations.literal: At this time, attacking Laizhou, Congzhi, Lian, and regional commander Yang Yufan and others divided the ramparts in defense.
translations.idiomatic: Now besieging Laizhou, the rebels found Xu Congzhi, Xie Lian, and regional commander Yang Yufan manning separate sections of the walls.

sentences.zh: 禦蕃，肇基子。

translations.literal: Yufan was Zhaoji's son.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yufan was the son of Yang Zhaoji.

sentences.zh: 肇基，從治所共剿滅妖賊鄒、滕者也。

translations.literal: Zhaoji was the one who together with Congzhi had exterminated the sorcerer-rebels at Zou and Teng.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zhaoji had fought alongside Xu Congzhi to wipe out the rebel cults at Zou and Teng.

sentences.zh: 禦蕃積戰功至通州副總兵。

translations.literal: Yufan, accumulating battle merit, rose to deputy regional commander at Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yufan had earned promotion to deputy regional commander at Tongzhou through repeated victories.

sentences.zh: 會登州陷，兵部尚書熊明遇奏署總兵官，盡將山東兵，與保定總兵劉國柱、天津總兵王洪兼程進。

translations.literal: As Dengzhou fell, Minister of War Xiong Mingyu memorialized appointing him acting regional commander, leading all Shandong troops together with Baoding regional commander Liu Guozhu and Tianjin regional commander Wang Hong to advance by forced marches.
translations.idiomatic: When Dengzhou fell, War Minister Xiong Mingyu named him acting regional commander and ordered him to march every Shandong soldier alongside Liu Guozhu of Baoding and Wang Hong of Tianjin at top speed.

sentences.zh: 遇賊新城，洪先走。

translations.literal: Encountering the rebels at Xincheng, Hong fled first.
translations.idiomatic: At Xincheng they met the rebels, and Wang Hong was the first to run.

sentences.zh: 禦蕃拒之二日，不勝，突圍出，遂入萊城，從治、璉倚以剿賊。

translations.literal: Yufan resisted for two days, could not prevail, broke out of encirclement, and entered Laizhou city; Congzhi and Lian relied on him to suppress the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yufan held them off for two days, then fought his way out and entered Laizhou, where Xu Congzhi and Xie Lian pinned their hopes on him to break the siege.

sentences.zh: 賊攻萊不下，分兵陷平度，知州陳所問自經。

translations.literal: The rebels could not take Laizhou and divided their forces to capture Pingdu; Prefect Chen Suowen hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to crack Laizhou, the rebels sent a detachment to seize Pingdu, where Prefect Chen Suowen hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 賊益攻萊，輦元化所制西洋大炮，日穴城，城多頹。

translations.literal: The rebels pressed harder on Laizhou, hauling out the Western cannon Yuanhua had made, daily mining under the walls; much of the city wall collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels redoubled their assault on Laizhou, deploying Sun Yuanhua's Western artillery and tunneling day after day until great stretches of wall crumbled.

sentences.zh: 從治等投火灌水，穴者死無算。

translations.literal: Congzhi and the others poured fire and water into the tunnels; those digging died beyond numbering.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Congzhi's defenders flooded the tunnels with fire and water, killing untold numbers of miners.

sentences.zh: 使死士時出掩擊之，毀其炮臺，斬獲多。

translations.literal: They sent dare-to-die soldiers out from time to time to strike by surprise, destroying their gun platforms and taking many heads and captives.
translations.idiomatic: Elite raiding parties sallied forth repeatedly, wrecking rebel gun emplacements and inflicting heavy casualties.

sentences.zh: 而明遇卒惑大成撫議也，命主事張國臣為贊畫往撫之，曰「安輯遼人之在山東者」，以國臣亦遼人也。

translations.literal: Yet Mingyu was ultimately swayed by Dacheng's pacification proposal; he ordered principal clerk Zhang Guochen as staff officer to go pacify them, saying "to settle the Liaodong men in Shandong," because Guochen was also a Liaodong man.
translations.idiomatic: But Xiong Mingyu had fallen under the spell of Yu Dacheng's appeasement policy; he dispatched staff officer Zhang Guochen to negotiate, declaring the mission was "to pacify the Liaodong troops in Shandong" — Guochen being a Liaodong native himself.

sentences.zh: 國臣先遣廢將金一鯨入賊營，已而國臣亦入，為賊移書，遣一鯨還報曰：「毋出兵壞撫局。」

translations.literal: Guochen first sent the dismissed general Jin Yijing into the rebel camp; soon Guochen also entered, drafted a letter for the rebels, and sent Yijing back to report: "Do not send troops and ruin the pacification arrangement."
translations.idiomatic: Guochen first sent the cashiered general Jin Yijing into the rebel camp, then entered himself and drafted letters on the rebels' behalf; Yijing returned with a message: "Send no troops — you will wreck the peace talks."

sentences.zh: 從治等知其詐，叱退一鯨，遣間使三上疏，言賊不可撫。

translations.literal: Congzhi and the others knew it was deceit; they reprimanded and dismissed Yijing, and sent secret messengers to submit three memorials, stating the rebels could not be pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Congzhi saw through the ruse, drove Jin Yijing away, and sent secret couriers bearing three memorials insisting the rebels could not be appeased.

sentences.zh: 最後言：「萊城被圍五十日，危如累卵。

translations.literal: The last stated: "Laizhou city has been besieged fifty days, perilous as piled eggs.
translations.idiomatic: The final memorial read: "Laizhou has been under siege for fifty days, balanced on a knife's edge.

sentences.zh: 日夜望援兵，卒不至，知必為撫議誤矣。

translations.literal: Day and night we await relief troops, yet in the end they do not come — we know we must have been misled by the pacification proposal.
translations.idiomatic: We watch day and night for relief that never arrives; we know the appeasement policy has doomed us.

sentences.zh: 國臣致書臣，內抄詔旨並兵部諭帖，乃知部臣已據國臣報，達聖聽。

translations.literal: Guochen sent a letter to this servant, enclosing copies of imperial edicts and War Ministry directives; only then did we know the ministry had based its reports on Guochen's dispatches and conveyed them to the sage ear.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guochen wrote me enclosing edicts and War Ministry orders — and only then did I learn the ministry had relayed his reports straight to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 夫國臣桑梓情重，忍欺聖明而陷封疆。

translations.literal: As for Guochen — his attachment to his native place runs deep; how could he bear to deceive the sage ruler and imperil the frontier?
translations.idiomatic: Guochen's loyalty to his homeland runs deep — how could he bear to lie to the throne and sacrifice the realm?

sentences.zh: 其初遣一鯨入賊營，何嘗有止兵不攻之事？

translations.literal: When he first sent Yijing into the rebel camp, was there ever any cessation of troops or halt to the attack?
translations.idiomatic: When he first sent Jin Yijing to the rebel camp, did the rebels ever once stop fighting?

sentences.zh: 果止兵，或稍退舍，臣等何故不樂撫？

translations.literal: If they had truly halted their army, or even retreated slightly, why would we servants not welcome pacification?
translations.idiomatic: If they had truly stood down — even pulled back a little — why would we oppose appeasement?

sentences.zh: 特國臣以撫為賊解，而賊實借撫為緩兵計。

translations.literal: Only Guochen treats pacification as releasing the rebels from their predicament — while the rebels in truth use pacification as a strategy to buy time.
translations.idiomatic: Guochen treats appeasement as a way to free the rebels — but the rebels use it purely to buy time.

sentences.zh: 一鯨受賊賄，對援師則誑言賊數萬，不可輕進；

translations.literal: Yijing took bribes from the rebels; to the relief army he lied that the rebels numbered tens of thousands and could not be lightly engaged;
translations.idiomatic: Jin Yijing took rebel bribes; to the relief force he lied that the rebels numbered in the tens of thousands and must not be engaged lightly;

sentences.zh: 對諸將則誑言賊用西洋炮攻，城將陷矣，賴我招撫，賊即止攻。

translations.literal: to the generals he lied that the rebels were attacking with Western cannon and the city was about to fall, but thanks to his summons to surrender, the rebels had ceased their assault.
translations.idiomatic: to the generals he claimed the rebels were battering the walls with Western artillery and the city was about to fall — but thanks to his negotiations, the rebels had halted their attack.

sentences.zh: 夫一鯨三入賊營，每入，賊攻益急。

translations.literal: Yijing entered the rebel camp three times; each time he entered, the rebel assault grew fiercer.
translations.idiomatic: Each of Jin Yijing's three visits to the rebel camp was followed by a fiercer assault.

sentences.zh: 而國臣乃雲賊嗔我縋城下擊，致彼之攻。

translations.literal: Yet Guochen said the rebels were angry that we lowered ourselves from the walls to strike them, provoking their attack.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Guochen claimed the rebels were angry because our men had sallied from the walls — provoking the onslaught.

sentences.zh: 是使賊任意攻擊，我不以一矢加遺，如元化斷送登城，然後可成國臣之撫耶？

translations.literal: So the rebels may attack at will while we do not shoot a single arrow — just as Yuanhua delivered up Dengzhou — and only then can Guochen's pacification succeed?
translations.idiomatic: Are we meant to let the rebels attack freely while we hold our fire — as Sun Yuanhua did before surrendering Dengzhou — so that Guochen's appeasement can succeed?

sentences.zh: 當賊過青州，大成擁兵三千，剿賊甚易。

translations.literal: When the rebels passed through Qingzhou, Dacheng held three thousand troops; suppressing the rebels would have been very easy.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels passed Qingzhou, Yu Dacheng had three thousand men at hand — crushing them would have been simple.

sentences.zh: 元化遺書謂『賊已就撫，爾兵毋東』，大成遂止勿追，致賊延蔓。

translations.literal: Yuanhua sent a letter saying "The rebels have already submitted to pacification; your troops must not move east"; Dacheng then halted and did not pursue, causing the rebels to spread.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yuanhua wrote that the rebels had accepted terms and ordered, "Do not march east"; Yu Dacheng stopped the pursuit, and the rebellion spread.

sentences.zh: 今賊視臣等猶元化，乃為賊解，曰吳橋激變有因也，一路封刀不殺也，聞天子詔遂止攻掠也。

translations.literal: Now the rebels regard us servants as they did Yuanhua, making excuses for the rebels, saying the Wuqiao incident had provocation behind it, that along the entire route swords were sheathed without killing, and that upon hearing the Son of Heaven's edict they ceased plundering.
translations.idiomatic: Now the rebels treat us as they treated Sun Yuanhua, spinning excuses: the Wuqiao mutiny had its provocation, they sheathed their swords all along the march, and they stopped looting once they heard the emperor's decree.

sentences.zh: 將誰欺！

translations.literal: Whom do they think they are deceiving!
translations.idiomatic: Who do they imagine they are fooling!

sentences.zh: 盈庭中國臣妄報，必謂一紙書賢於十萬兵，援師不來，職是故矣。

translations.literal: At court Guochen's false reports prevail; they must believe one sheet of paper is worth more than a hundred thousand troops — relief does not come, and that is precisely the reason.
translations.idiomatic: At court Guochen's lies hold sway; they must think one letter outweighs a hundred thousand soldiers — and that is exactly why no relief has come.

sentences.zh: 臣死當為厲鬼以殺賊，斷不敢以撫謾至尊，淆國是，誤封疆，而戕生命也。」

translations.literal: When this servant dies I shall become a vengeful ghost to slay the rebels; I dare not use pacification to deceive the supreme sovereign, confuse the nation's policy, mislead the frontier, and squander lives."
translations.idiomatic: If I die, I will return as a vengeful ghost to kill these rebels; I will never use appeasement to deceive the throne, muddy national policy, betray the frontier, and waste lives."

sentences.zh: 疏入，未報。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted; no reply came.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial reached the throne; no answer followed.

sentences.zh: 當是時，外圍日急，國柱、洪及山東援軍俱頓昌邑不敢進，兩撫臣困圍城中。

translations.literal: At that time the outer encirclement grew daily tighter; Guozhu, Hong, and the Shandong relief troops all halted at Changyi and dared not advance; the two grand coordinators were trapped inside the besieged city.
translations.idiomatic: By then the siege was tightening daily; Liu Guozhu, Wang Hong, and every Shandong relief column stalled at Changyi, afraid to advance, while both grand coordinators were trapped inside Laizhou.

sentences.zh: 於是廷議更設總督一人，以兵部右侍郎劉宇烈任之。

translations.literal: Thereupon the court deliberated and established an additional post of governor-general, assigning Minister of War Right Vice Minister Liu Yulie to it.
translations.idiomatic: The court then created a new governor-generalship and appointed War Vice Minister Liu Yulie to the post.

sentences.zh: 調薊門、四川兵，統以總兵鄧玘，調密雲兵，統以副將牟文綬，以右布政使楊作楫監之，往援萊。

translations.literal: Troops from Jimen and Sichuan were mobilized under regional commander Deng Qi; troops from Miyun under deputy general Mou Wenshou; Right Administration Commissioner Yang Zuoji was appointed to supervise them — all to relieve Laizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Qi was given Jimen and Sichuan troops; Mou Wenshou took command of Miyun forces; Administration Commissioner Yang Zuoji was sent to oversee them — all marching to relieve Laizhou.

sentences.zh: 三月，宇烈、作楫、國柱、洪、玘及監視中官呂直，巡按御史王道純，義勇副將劉澤清，新兵參將劉永昌、朱廷祿，監紀推官汪惟效等並集昌邑。

translations.literal: In the third month, Yulie, Zuoji, Guozhu, Hong, Qi, and supervising eunuch Lü Zhi, investigating censor Wang Daochun, volunteer deputy general Liu Zeqing, new-troop brigade commanders Liu Yongchang and Zhu Tinglu, supervising registrar Wang Weixiao, and others all assembled at Changyi.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Liu Yulie, Yang Zuoji, Liu Guozhu, Wang Hong, Deng Qi, the supervising eunuch Lü Zhi, Censor Wang Daochun, Liu Zeqing, Liu Yongchang, Zhu Tinglu, Registrar Wang Weixiao, and a host of others gathered at Changyi.

sentences.zh: 玘、國柱、洪、澤清等至萊州，馬步軍二萬五千，氣甚盛。

translations.literal: Qi, Guozhu, Hong, Zeqing, and the others reached Laizhou with twenty-five thousand cavalry and infantry; their morale was very high.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Qi, Liu Guozhu, Wang Hong, Liu Zeqing, and their combined force of twenty-five thousand horse and foot reached Laizhou in high spirits.

sentences.zh: 而宇烈無籌略，諸師懦怯，抵沙河，日十輩往議撫，縱還所獲賊陳文才。

translations.literal: Yet Yulie had no strategy; the armies were cowardly; reaching Shahe, ten parties a day went to negotiate pacification, and they released the captured rebel Chen Wencai.
translations.idiomatic: But Liu Yulie had no strategy and his commanders were timid; at Shahe they sent ten delegations a day to negotiate appeasement and even freed the captured rebel Chen Wencai.

sentences.zh: 於是賊盡得我虛實，益以撫愚我，而潛兵繞其後，盡焚我輜重。

translations.literal: The rebels thus learned all our strengths and weaknesses; they further used pacification to deceive us, while secretly sending troops around our rear and burning all our baggage train.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels learned every detail of our strength, played for time with feigned talks, sent troops around our rear, and burned our entire supply train.

sentences.zh: 宇烈懼，遂走青州，撤三將兵就食。

translations.literal: Yulie grew afraid and fled to Qingzhou, ordering the three generals' troops to go for provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yulie panicked, fled to Qingzhou, and dispersed his three generals to forage for food.

sentences.zh: 玘等夜半拔營散，賊乘之，大敗。

translations.literal: Qi and the others broke camp and scattered at midnight; the rebels seized the moment and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Qi and the others broke camp and scattered at midnight; the rebels struck and routed them utterly.

sentences.zh: 洪、國柱走青、濰，玘走昌邑，澤清接戰於萊城，傷二指，亦敗走平度，惟作楫能軍。

translations.literal: Hong and Guozhu fled toward Qing and Wei; Qi fled to Changyi; Zeqing joined battle at Laizhou city, losing two fingers, and also fled defeated to Pingdu — only Zuoji could fight.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hong and Liu Guozhu fled toward Qingzhou and Weifang; Deng Qi retreated to Changyi; Liu Zeqing fought at Laizhou, lost two fingers, and was driven back to Pingdu — only Yang Zuoji distinguished himself in battle.

sentences.zh: 三將既敗，舉朝嘩然，而明遇見官軍不可用，撫議益堅。

translations.literal: Once the three generals were defeated, the whole court was in uproar; yet Mingyu, seeing the government troops were unusable, grew firmer in the pacification proposal.
translations.idiomatic: After the three generals' rout the court erupted in alarm — yet Xiong Mingyu, convinced the army was useless, doubled down on appeasement.

sentences.zh: 先是，登州總兵可大死，以副將吳安邦代之，安邦尤怯鈍。

translations.literal: Earlier, Dengzhou regional commander Keda had died; deputy general Wu Anbang replaced him — Anbang was especially timid and dull.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhang Keda's death, the inept and timid Wu Anbang replaced him as Dengzhou regional commander.

sentences.zh: 奉令屯寧海，規取登州。

translations.literal: Ordered to encamp at Ninghai, he planned to retake Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to encamp at Ninghai, he planned an assault on Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 仲明揚言以城降，安邦信之，離城二十五里而軍。

translations.literal: Zhongming proclaimed he would surrender the city; Anbang believed him and encamped twenty-five li from the city.
translations.idiomatic: Geng Zhongming announced he would surrender the city; Wu Anbang believed him and camped twenty-five li away.

sentences.zh: 中軍徐樹聲薄城被擒，安邦走還寧海。

translations.literal: Headquarters officer Xu Shusheng approached the walls and was captured; Anbang fled back to Ninghai.
translations.idiomatic: When headquarters officer Xu Shusheng approached the walls he was captured; Wu Anbang fled back to Ninghai.

sentences.zh: 登既不能下，而賊困萊久，璉、從治、禦蕃日堅守待救。

translations.literal: Deng could not be taken; meanwhile the rebels had long besieged Laizhou; Lian, Congzhi, and Yufan daily held firm awaiting rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Dengzhou could not be retaken, and as the siege of Laizhou dragged on, Xie Lian, Xu Congzhi, and Yang Yufan held the walls day after day, waiting for rescue.

sentences.zh: 至四月十六日，從治中炮死，萊人大臨，守陴者皆哭。

translations.literal: On the sixteenth day of the fourth month, Congzhi was killed by cannon fire; the people of Laizhou wailed in grief, and all those defending the ramparts wept.
translations.idiomatic: On the sixteenth of the fourth month Xu Congzhi was killed by cannon fire; Laizhou wept as one, and every defender on the walls broke down in tears.

sentences.zh: 山東士官南京者，合疏攻宇烈，請益兵。

translations.literal: Shandong officials in Nanjing jointly submitted a memorial attacking Yulie and requesting additional troops.
translations.idiomatic: Shandong officials stationed in Nanjing submitted a joint memorial denouncing Liu Yulie and demanding reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 於是調昌平兵三千，以總兵陳洪範統之，洪範亦遼人。

translations.literal: Changping troops numbering three thousand were then mobilized under regional commander Chen Hongfan's command — Hongfan was also a Liaodong man.
translations.idiomatic: Three thousand Changping troops were mobilized under regional commander Chen Hongfan — another native of Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 明遇日跂望曰：「往哉，其可撫也。」

translations.literal: Mingyu daily looked on eagerly and said: "Go — they can be pacified."
translations.idiomatic: Xiong Mingyu watched eagerly and said, "Go — they can still be appeased."

sentences.zh: 天津舊將孫應龍者，大言於眾曰：「仲明兄弟與我善，我能令其縛有德、九成來。」

translations.literal: Among them was Tianjin's former general Sun Yinglong, who boasted to the crowd: "The Zhongming brothers and I are on good terms; I can make them bind Youde and Jiucheng and deliver them."
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yinglong, a former Tianjin general, boasted to the assembly: "The Zhongming brothers are my friends — I can have them bind Kong Youde and Li Jiucheng and deliver them."

sentences.zh: 巡撫鄭宗周予之兵二千，從海道往。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Zheng Zongzhou gave him two thousand troops to go by sea route.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Zheng Zongzhou gave him two thousand men and sent him by sea.

sentences.zh: 仲明聞之，偽函他死人頭紿之曰：「此有德也。」

translations.literal: Zhongming heard of this and sent a false package with another dead man's head, deceiving him, saying: "This is Youde."
translations.idiomatic: Geng Zhongming heard of the mission and sent a severed head from another corpse, claiming: "This is Kong Youde."

sentences.zh: 應龍率舟師抵水城。

translations.literal: Yinglong led his naval force to arrive at Shuicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yinglong sailed his fleet to Shuicheng.

sentences.zh: 延之入，猝縛斬之，無一人脫者。

translations.literal: They invited him in, suddenly bound and beheaded him — not a single man escaped.
translations.idiomatic: They lured him ashore, bound him, and executed him — not one man escaped.

sentences.zh: 賊得巨艦，勢益張。

translations.literal: The rebels obtained great ships; their power grew more overbearing.
translations.idiomatic: With great warships in hand, the rebels' power swelled.

sentences.zh: 島帥黃龍攻之不克而還。

translations.literal: Island commander Huang Long attacked but could not overcome them and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Island commander Huang Long attacked but failed and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 遂破招遠，圍萊陽。

translations.literal: They then stormed Zhaoyuan and besieged Laiyang.
translations.idiomatic: They overran Zhaoyuan and laid siege to Laiyang.

sentences.zh: 知縣梁衡固守，賊敗去。

translations.literal: Magistrate Liang Heng held firm in defense; the rebels were defeated and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate Liang Heng held the city; the rebels were beaten off.

sentences.zh: 宇烈復至昌邑，洪範、文綬等亦至。

translations.literal: Yulie again arrived at Changyi; Hongfan, Wenshou, and others also arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yulie returned to Changyi, joined by Chen Hongfan, Mou Wenshou, and others.

sentences.zh: 萊州推官屈宜陽請入賊營講撫，賊佯禮之。

translations.literal: Laizhou Registrar Qu Yiyang requested to enter the rebel camp to negotiate pacification; the rebels feigned courtesy toward him.
translations.idiomatic: Laizhou Registrar Qu Yiyang volunteered to enter the rebel camp to negotiate; the rebels treated him with false civility.

sentences.zh: 宜陽使言賊已受命，宇烈奏得請，乃手書諭賊令解圍。

translations.literal: Yiyang sent word that the rebels had already received imperial authorization; Yulie memorialized that permission was granted, and then personally wrote instructing the rebels to lift the siege.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Yiyang reported the rebels had received imperial sanction; Liu Yulie memorialized for approval and personally wrote ordering them to lift the siege.

sentences.zh: 賊邀宇烈，宇烈懼不往。

translations.literal: The rebels invited Yulie; Yulie was afraid and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels summoned Liu Yulie, but he was too frightened to go.

sentences.zh: 營將嚴正中舁龍亭及河，賊擁之去，而令宜陽還萊，文武官出城開讀，圍即解。

translations.literal: Camp commander Yan Zhengzhong carried the dragon pavilion to the river; the rebels seized it and took it away, while ordering Yiyang to return to Laizhou — if civil and military officials came out of the city to read the proclamation aloud, the siege would immediately be lifted.
translations.idiomatic: Camp commander Yan Zhengzhong carried the imperial pavilion to the riverbank; the rebels seized it, sent Qu Yiyang back to Laizhou, and promised to lift the siege if officials came out to read the proclamation aloud.

sentences.zh: 禦蕃不可，璉曰：「圍且六月，既已無可奈何，宜且從之。」

translations.literal: Yufan would not agree; Lian said: "The siege has lasted nearly six months; since there is already nothing to be done, we ought for now to comply."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yufan refused; Xie Lian said, "The siege has lasted nearly six months — we have no choice but to comply for now."

sentences.zh: 遂偕監視中官徐得時、翟升，知府朱萬年出。

translations.literal: Thereupon together with supervising eunuchs Xu Deshi and Zhai Sheng, and Prefect Zhu Wannian, they went out.
translations.idiomatic: So he went out with the supervising eunuchs Xu Deshi and Zhai Sheng and Prefect Zhu Wannian.

sentences.zh: 有德等叩頭扶伏，涕泣交頤，璉慰諭久之而還。

translations.literal: Youde and the others kowtowed and prostrated themselves, tears streaming down their faces; Lian comforted and instructed them at length and then returned.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Youde and the others kowtowed and prostrated themselves, weeping; Xie Lian reassured them at length and returned inside.

sentences.zh: 明日復令宜陽入，請璉、禦蕃同出。

translations.literal: The next day they again sent Yiyang in, requesting Lian and Yufan to come out together.
translations.idiomatic: The next day they sent Qu Yiyang back to summon Xie Lian and Yang Yufan outside the walls.

sentences.zh: 禦蕃曰：「我將家子，知殺賊，何知撫事？」

translations.literal: Yufan said: "I am a general's son — I know how to kill rebels; what do I know of pacification affairs?"
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yufan replied, "I am a soldier's son — I know how to kill rebels, not how to negotiate surrender."

sentences.zh: 璉等遂出。

translations.literal: Lian and the others then went out.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Lian and the others went out nonetheless.

sentences.zh: 有德執之，猝攻城，卻令萬年呼降。

translations.literal: Youde seized them, suddenly assaulted the city, and ordered Wannian to call for surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Youde seized them, launched a sudden assault, and forced Zhu Wannian to shout for the city to surrender.

sentences.zh: 萬年呼曰：「吾死矣，汝等宜固守。」

translations.literal: Wannian shouted: "I am dead already — you all ought to hold firm in defense."
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Wannian cried out, "I am already dead — hold the walls!"

sentences.zh: 罵不絕口而死。

translations.literal: He cursed without cease until he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died cursing without pause.

sentences.zh: 賊送璉及二中官至登囚之，正中、宜陽皆死。

translations.literal: The rebels sent Lian and the two eunuchs to Deng to imprison them; Zhengzhong and Yiyang both died.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels sent Xie Lian and the two eunuchs to Deng and imprisoned them; Yan Zhengzhong and Qu Yiyang were both killed.

sentences.zh: 初，撫議興，獨從治持不可。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the pacification proposal arose, Congzhi alone maintained it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: When the appeasement policy first took hold, Xu Congzhi alone stood against it.

sentences.zh: 宇烈諸將信之，而尚書明遇主其議。

translations.literal: Yulie and the generals believed in it, while Minister Mingyu chaired the proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yulie and his generals believed in it; War Minister Xiong Mingyu championed the policy.

sentences.zh: 從治死，璉遂被擒。

translations.literal: Congzhi died, and Lian was then captured.
translations.idiomatic: With Congzhi dead, Lian was taken prisoner.

sentences.zh: 於是舉朝恚憤，逮宇烈下獄，調關外勁卒剿之，罷總督及登萊巡撫不設，專任代從治者朱大典以行。

translations.literal: Thereupon the whole court burned with indignation; Liu Yulie was arrested and imprisoned, crack troops from beyond the passes were transferred to suppress the rebels, the posts of supreme commander and Deng-Lai grand coordinator were abolished, and Zhu Dadian alone was entrusted to act in Congzhi's place.
translations.idiomatic: The whole court burned with indignation. Liu Yulie was thrown into prison, tough troops from beyond the passes were brought in to crush the rebels, the supreme command and the Deng-Lai grand coordinator's post were abolished, and only Zhu Dadian was left to carry on Congzhi's work.

sentences.zh: 明遇坐主撫誤國，罷歸，遂絕撫議。

translations.literal: Xiong Mingyu was punished for championing appeasement and misleading the state, dismissed and sent home, and the policy of appeasement was ended for good.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong Mingyu was punished for having championed appeasement and misled the state, dismissed and sent home, and the appeasement policy was ended for good.

sentences.zh: 八月，大典合兵救萊。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Dadian combined his forces to relieve Laizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Zhu Dadian united his armies to break the siege of Laizhou.

sentences.zh: 兵甫接，賊輒大敗，圍解。

translations.literal: As soon as the armies engaged, the rebels were utterly defeated and the siege was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: At the first clash the rebels were routed and the siege was raised.

sentences.zh: 有德走登州，九成殺璉及二中官。

translations.literal: Youde fled to Dengzhou; Jiucheng killed Lian and the two eunuch supervisors.
translations.idiomatic: Youde fled to Dengzhou, where Jiucheng killed Lian and the two supervising eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 大典圍登，九成戰死。

translations.literal: Dadian besieged Dengzhou, and Jiucheng died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Dadian laid siege to Dengzhou, and Jiucheng fell in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 城破，追剿，有德、仲明入海遁。

translations.literal: When the city fell they pursued the rebels; Youde and Zhongming escaped by sea.
translations.idiomatic: After the city fell they pursued the rebels; Youde and Zhongming fled by sea.

sentences.zh: 生擒承祿等，斬應元，賊盡平。

translations.literal: Chenglu and others were captured alive, Yingyuan was beheaded, and the rebels were entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Chenglu and others were captured alive, Yingyuan was beheaded, and the rebellion was entirely suppressed.

sentences.zh: 事詳《大典傳》。

translations.literal: The affair is treated in detail in the biography of Dadian.
translations.idiomatic: The affair is treated in detail in Dadian's biography.

sentences.zh: 詔贈從治兵部尚書，賜祭葬，蔭錦衣百戶，建祠曰「忠烈」；

translations.literal: An edict posthumously honored Congzhi as minister of War, granted sacrificial rites and burial, enfeoffed a hundred households in the Embroidered Uniform Guard, and erected a shrine called "Loyal and Steadfast";
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously honored Congzhi as minister of War, granted him sacrificial rites and a state burial, enfeoffed a hundred households in the Embroidered Uniform Guard, and erected a shrine called Loyal and Steadfast;

sentences.zh: 贈璉兵部右侍郎，亦賜祭葬，建祠，蔭子；

translations.literal: Lian was posthumously honored as vice minister of War, likewise granted sacrificial rites and burial, given a shrine, and his son enfeoffed;
translations.idiomatic: Lian was posthumously made vice minister of War, granted sacrificial rites and burial, given a shrine, and his son received an enfeoffment;

sentences.zh: 以禦蕃功多，加署都督同知，總兵，鎮登、萊。

translations.literal: because Yufan's merits were many, he was given acting rank as commissioner-in-chief of the right, made regional commander, and stationed at Deng and Lai.
translations.idiomatic: Because Yufan's merits were great, he was given acting rank as commissioner-in-chief of the right, made regional commander, and stationed at Deng and Lai.

sentences.zh: 而宇烈以次年遣戍。

translations.literal: Yulie was sent into exile the next year.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Yulie was banished.

sentences.zh: 璉，字君實，監利人。

translations.literal: Lian, style Junshi, was a native of Jianli.
translations.idiomatic: Lian, whose style name was Junshi, came from Jianli.

sentences.zh: 宇烈，綿竹人，大學士宇亮兄也。

translations.literal: Yulie was a native of Mianzhu and elder brother of Grand Secretary Yuliang.
translations.idiomatic: Yulie came from Mianzhu and was the elder brother of Grand Secretary Yuliang.

sentences.zh: 其戍也，人以為失刑。

translations.literal: When he was exiled, people thought the punishment did not fit the crime.
translations.idiomatic: When he was exiled, many thought the punishment did not fit the crime.

sentences.zh: 大成逮下獄，遣戍。

translations.literal: Dacheng was arrested and imprisoned and sent into exile.
translations.idiomatic: Dacheng was thrown into prison and then banished.

sentences.zh: 赦還，卒於家。

translations.literal: After an amnesty he returned but died at home.
translations.idiomatic: After an amnesty he returned home but died there.

sentences.zh: 元化，字初陽，嘉定人。

translations.literal: Yuanhua, style Chuyang, was a native of Jiading.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yuanhua, whose style name was Chuyang, came from Jiading.

sentences.zh: 天啟間舉於鄉。

translations.literal: In the Tianqi period he passed the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianqi reign he passed the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 所善西洋炮法，蓋得之徐光啟雲。

translations.literal: He was skilled in Western artillery methods, which he is said to have learned from Xu Guangqi.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered Western artillery methods, said to have been learned from Xu Guangqi.

sentences.zh: 廣寧覆沒，條備京、防邊二策。

translations.literal: When Guangning was lost he submitted two plans for defending the capital and the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of Guangning he submitted two plans for defending the capital and the frontier.

sentences.zh: 孫承宗請於朝，得贊畫經略軍前。

translations.literal: Sun Chengzong petitioned the court on his behalf, and he was made planning officer on the staff of the frontier commander.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Chengzong recommended him at court, and he was appointed planning officer on the frontier commander's staff.

sentences.zh: 主建炮臺教練法，因請據寧遠、前屯，以策幹王在晉，在晉不能用。

translations.literal: He advocated building gun platforms and drill methods, and therefore asked to hold Ningyuan and Qiantun, memorializing against Wang Zaijin, who could not employ his plan.
translations.idiomatic: He advocated building gun platforms and training methods, and therefore urged holding Ningyuan and Qiantun, memorializing against Wang Zaijin, who would not adopt his plan.

sentences.zh: 承宗行邊，還奏，授兵部司務。

translations.literal: Chengzong toured the frontier and, on returning, memorialized; Yuanhua was appointed clerk in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzong toured the frontier and, on returning, memorialized the throne; Yuanhua was appointed clerk in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 承宗代在晉，遂破重關之非，築臺制炮，一如元化言。

translations.literal: When Chengzong replaced Zaijin he refuted the error of abandoning the key passes, built platforms and controlled artillery exactly as Yuanhua had urged.
translations.idiomatic: When Chengzong replaced Zaijin he refuted the folly of abandoning the key passes, building platforms and deploying artillery exactly as Yuanhua had urged.

sentences.zh: 還授元化職方主事，已，元化贊畫袁崇煥寧遠。

translations.literal: On returning he appointed Yuanhua chief clerk in the Bureau of Military Appointments; later Yuanhua served as planning officer under Yuan Chonghuan at Ningyuan.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he made Yuanhua chief clerk in the Bureau of Military Appointments; Yuanhua later served as planning officer under Yuan Chonghuan at Ningyuan.

sentences.zh: 還朝，尋罷。

translations.literal: He returned to court and was soon dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to the capital but was soon dismissed.

sentences.zh: 崇禎初，起武選員外郎，進職方郎中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chongzhen he was raised as vice director in the Bureau of Military Selection and promoted to bureau director.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Chongzhen reign he was raised in the Bureau of Military Selection and promoted to bureau director.

sentences.zh: 崇煥已為經略，乞元化自輔，遂改元化山東右參議，整飭寧前兵備。

translations.literal: Chonghuan was already frontier commissioner and begged Yuanhua to assist him; Yuanhua was therefore made right vice commissioner of Shandong to organize Ningqian military defense.
translations.idiomatic: Chonghuan was already frontier commissioner and asked that Yuanhua assist him; Yuanhua was therefore transferred to right vice commissioner of Shandong to organize Ningqian defenses.

sentences.zh: 三年，皮島副將劉興治為亂，廷議復設登萊巡撫，遂擢元化右僉都御史任之，駐登州。

translations.literal: In the third year the Pidao deputy commander Liu Xingzhi mutinied; the court debated restoring the Deng-Lai grand coordinator's post and therefore promoted Yuanhua to right vice censor-in-chief to fill it, stationed at Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Pidao deputy commander Liu Xingzhi mutinied; the court debated restoring the Deng-Lai grand coordinator and promoted Yuanhua to right vice censor-in-chief at Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 明年，島眾殺興治，元化奏副將黃龍代，汰其兵六千人。

translations.literal: The next year the island troops killed Xingzhi; Yuanhua memorialized that Deputy Commander Huang Long replace him and cut six thousand of his troops.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the island garrison killed Xingzhi; Yuanhua memorialized that Huang Long replace him as deputy commander and cut six thousand troops.

sentences.zh: 及有德反，朝野由是怨元化之不能討也。

translations.literal: When Youde rebelled, court and country alike blamed Yuanhua for failing to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: Once Youde rebelled, everyone at court and in the country blamed Yuanhua for failing to put him down.

sentences.zh: 賊縱元化還，詔逮之。

translations.literal: The rebels released Yuanhua; an edict ordered his arrest.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels let Yuanhua go; an edict then ordered his arrest.

sentences.zh: 首輔周延儒謀脫其死，不得也；

translations.literal: Chief Minister Zhou Yanru tried to save him from death but could not;
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Zhou Yanru tried to secure his life but failed;

sentences.zh: 則援其師光啟入閣圖之，卒不得，同張燾棄市。

translations.literal: he then appealed through his teacher Guangqi's entry into the cabinet, but still failed; Yuanhua was executed in the marketplace together with Zhang Tao.
translations.idiomatic: he then tried to use his teacher Guangqi's entry into the cabinet to save him, but still failed; Yuanhua was executed in the marketplace together with Zhang Tao.

sentences.zh: 光蘭、征充軍。

translations.literal: Guanglan and Zheng were sentenced to military exile.
translations.idiomatic: Guanglan and Zheng were banished to military service on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：疆圉多故，則思任事之臣。

translations.literal: The appraiser says: When the frontier is beset with many troubles, one longs for officials who will shoulder responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: When the frontier is in turmoil, one longs for men who will take responsibility.

sentences.zh: 梅之煥諸人，風采機略尚大異於巽懦恇怯之徒，而牽於文法，或廢或死，悲夫！

translations.literal: Men such as Mei Zhihuan still differed greatly in spirit and resourcefulness from the timid and craven, yet bound by formal rules they were either dismissed or put to death—how lamentable!
translations.idiomatic: Men such as Mei Zhihuan were still worlds apart in spirit and resourcefulness from the timid and craven, yet bound by formal rules they were either dismissed or put to death—how lamentable!

sentences.zh: 叛將衡行，縛而斬之，一偏裨力耳。

translations.literal: When rebel generals ran riot, binding and beheading them was no more than the strength of a single junior officer.
translations.idiomatic: When rebel generals ran riot, binding and beheading them was work a single junior officer could do.

sentences.zh: 中撓撫議，委堅城畀之，援師觀望不進，徒擾擾焉。

translations.literal: Yet at the center appeasement was undermined, strong cities were handed over, and relief armies stood by without advancing—only to bustle about in vain.
translations.idiomatic: Yet at court appeasement was undermined, strong cities were handed over, and relief armies stood by without advancing—only to bustle about in vain.

sentences.zh: 設官命將，何益之有？

translations.literal: What good did it do to set up offices and appoint generals?
translations.idiomatic: Of what use was it to create offices and appoint generals?

sentences.zh: 撫議之誤國也，可勝言哉！

translations.literal: The harm done to the state by the policy of appeasement—can it be told in full?
translations.idiomatic: The harm the appeasement policy did the state—can it even be told in full?
